sessions.title: GHC POWER UP
sessions.abstract:
Morning Movement for Stronger Bodies, Sharper Minds & Better Days 

Before the sessions start, the meetings begin, and the ideas start flowing, take 45 minutes for you. 

GHC Power Up is a new morning movement series designed to help attendees start the day feeling energized, grounded, and ready to take on GHC. Across three mornings, attendees can choose from yoga, HIIT, and full-body fitness experiences led by dynamic wellness instructors Reina Dominguez and Paris Jackson. 

Because showing up as your best self isn't just about what you know. It's also about taking care of the body and mind that make everything else possible. 

Whether you want to stretch, sweat, reset, or simply make space for yourself before a full conference day, Power Up is your invitation to move. 

Wednesday | POWER UP: Cardio Dance with Paris Jackson, Founder of Sweat Sessions 

Kick off GHC with energy. Join Coach P for a high-energy Cardio Dance workout combining upbeat music, rhythmic movement, and muscle-focused exercises for a full-body, feel-good fitness experience. 

Participants will dance, groove, and sweat through movements designed to elevate the heart rate and work the body from head to toe. No dance experience is required, and the class is designed for all fitness levels. 

Thursday | GHC POWER UP: HIIT Reset with Reina Dominguez, Founder of The Inner Edge Training 

Turn up the energy before the conference day begins. This high-energy fitness experience is designed to get your heart pumping, challenge your body, and build strength while allowing participants to work at their own level. 

Reina brings more than 15 years of experience in intentional movement and combines functional fitness, performance coaching, and an inclusive approach designed to leave participants feeling energized, capable, and connected. 

Friday | GHC POWER UP: Flow State with Reina Dominguez, Founder of The Inner Edge Training 

Close out GHC with Flow State, a mindful yoga flow designed to improve mobility, release tension, and reconnect mind and body. 

Through intentional movement and breathwork, participants will build space, restore balance, and leave feeling grounded, energized, and ready for the day ahead.

sessions.title: Is IP Right for You? Women Leaders Share Real‑World Paths in Patents
sessions.abstract:
“Is IP Right for You?” invites women in tech into a candid conversation about real career paths in intellectual property, from patent architect to patent attorney. With a moderator leading the way, three women representing in-house, law firm, and technical IP roles will reveal both their success stories and the real tradeoffs they face in workload, advancement, connection to technology, and worklife boundaries.
Panelists will share their journeys into IP, walk through a day in the life, and discuss what they find most energizing and challenging. They will also examine how core skills like curiosity about technology, comfort with ambiguity, strong communication, advocacy, and resilience are valued differently in each setting. Attendees will gain practical insight on how to break into IP from technical careers, how to choose among law firm, in-house, and technical IP tracks, how to grow into leadership, and concrete next steps to explore IP after Grace Hopper.

sessions.title: Agentic AI in Pharma & Life Sciences: Designing Trustworthy AI for High-Stakes Decisions
sessions.abstract:
Generative AI is rapidly evolving, yet in pharma and life sciences, adoption requires more than impressive outputs, it requires trust. Decisions in these domains affect patient outcomes, regulatory compliance, and high-stakes business strategy, making transparency and accountability essential.

This session introduces agentic AI, an approach where multiple AI agents collaborate to plan tasks, reason step by step, use tools responsibly, and involve humans at key decision points. sessions.title: An Actionable Plan for Your First 30/60/90 Days/Weeks/Months
sessions.abstract:
Starting a new job can be exciting, but honestly, also scary. Inner monologue kicks in immediately: "Am I qualified?" "When will they figure out I don't know what I'm doing?" "What should I even be focusing on right now?" We say this to ourselves, but rarely aloud. Feeling like you’re not enough, imposter syndrome, and finding your place in work are real; the feelings don't discriminate by experience. Whether you're landing your first role or pivoting into leadership, the unknowns can be overwhelming. You may look up one day and realize weeks have passed without clear direction, or worse, that you've been working on the wrong things entirely.
The goal of this session is to change the cycle of self-doubt, lack of direction, and quiet struggle to help attendees find their footing. Through goal setting and open dialogue, we will discuss practical milestones for those critical early weeks and months in a new position, and strategies for navigating ambiguity when no one hands you a roadmap.

sessions.title: Agentic AI in Enterprises: From Fundamentals to Production Implementation
sessions.abstract:
Agentic AI is rapidly transforming enterprises, shifting the paradigm from reactive chatbot deployments to autonomous, goal-driven systems capable of reasoning, planning, and acting across complex business workflows. While early enterprise AI initiatives focused on conversational interfaces and scripted automation, a new class of systems is emerging intelligent agents that combine large language models with memory, tools, planning strategies, and orchestration frameworks to execute multi-step tasks with minimal human intervention. These systems are not merely answering questions; they are achieving objectives.

What makes this moment particularly critical is the pace of change facing developers and architects building these systems. The agentic tooling ecosystem—spanning frameworks like LangGraph, AutoGen, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP)is evolving at a rate that demands continuous adaptation. Developers must now navigate shifting abstractions, rapidly deprecating APIs, and emerging patterns such as multi-agent orchestration, tool calling standardization, and dynamic memory architectures. Adaptability is no longer a soft skill; it is a core engineering competency. In this technical talk, Agentic AI in Enterprises: From Fundamentals to Production Implementation, we take a structured journey from first principles to fully operational enterprise systems delivering measurable return on investment. The session begins by establishing a clear conceptual foundation for what makes an AI system "agentic" and how developers can build systems that remain resilient and maintainable as the underlying models, protocols, and platforms continue to evolve beneath them.

sessions.title: Beyond LeetCode: Building a Career That Outlasts the Hype
sessions.abstract:
The era of the "code typist" is ending. While mastering data structures remains a core requirement for entry, thriving at tech companies now requires a radical shift in mindset. As industry workflows transition from manual coding to directing AI agents, the value of a Software Engineer is shifting from syntax knowledge to high-level reasoning and system design.

In this session, we will explore the shift from a programmer to architect. We move beyond simple code completion to explore agentic AI workflows while witnessing success as a software engineer in our new augmented landscape. This transformation is especially relevant for students, new graduates, and early-career engineers navigating a rapidly changing technology market.

Bringing together engineers from Google, Microsoft, Meta, and NVIDIA, this panel offers a cross-industry view of how engineering careers are evolving in a fast-paced world across different roles, organizations, and technical domains.

This session features a structured discussion on how engineers can build durable careers, maintain long-term technical impact, remain grounded in fundamentals, and responsibly leverage emerging tools to adapt to a rapidly evolving technology landscape. We will explore the following themes:

I. The Shift: From Programmer to Architect

a. Why the software engineer role is evolving: Moving from "how to write" to "what to build."

b. Core Hypothesis: If you want to build a career that lasts, resilience starts with how you build skills, adapt to change, and plan for long-term growth.

II. Responsibility & Quality Control

a. The Engineer as the Guardian: Preventing algorithmic bias and ensuring security.

b. Practical methodologies for testing AI-assisted code.

c. Quality is no longer just about whether code runs. It is about whether the system can be trusted.

III. Building a Foundation That Outlasts Hype

a. Why data structures still matter (the "logic" behind the AI).

b. Developing the "Architect’s Eye": Focus on system design, scalability, and code quality.

c. The future belongs to engineers who can combine speed with depth, using automation without becoming dependent on it.

Why This Session?

For students, new graduates, and early-career engineers, the tech market can feel uncertain. AI is changing how software is built, and many people are wondering what skills will still matter. This session turns that uncertainty into a clear strategy.

Instead of viewing AI as a replacement, we will explore how engineers can use it as a powerful tool to move faster, think bigger, and focus on higher-value work. The goal is to help attendees grow from simply writing code to thinking like architects: people who understand problems deeply, make strong technical decisions, validate results, and take ownership of systems.

Attendees will leave with a practical mindset for building careers that can adapt, sustain, and grow through the next decade of technological change.

Key Learning Objectives :

a. The Foundation: Understand why "LeetCode" skills are the baseline, but "System Thinking" is the differentiator for long-term career growth in Big Tech.

b. Work Smarter with AI: Learn how to pivot from writing raw code to orchestrating AI agents that handle mundane tasks, redefining your personal productivity.

c. Be an Architect: Learn how to review, test, and improve AI-generated work instead of blindly trusting it. This includes setting guardrails, checking security risks, reducing bias, and making sure software is reliable and maintainable.

sessions.title: Get Hired : Practical Ways to Get Seen as Hiring Marketplaces become Agentic
sessions.abstract:
Hiring has moved beyond “post and pray/apply and wait.”
Today, your profile often acts as a 24/7 passive application as hiring increasingly happens through talent marketplaces and proactive sourcing, not just job applications.
Think navigation apps: they don’t give everyone the same route. They adapt to live signals like traffic, delays, and detours to help you reach your destination.
Modern hiring works similarly, responding to signals like clarity, alignment, credibility, responsiveness, follow-through. Two similar résumés can see very different outcomes depending on how clearly those signals show up.
Based on patterns observed in real hiring workflows, ATSs and talent marketplaces, this session shows practical ways to strengthen those signals, how recruiters use assistive workflows without automating decisions or replacing human judgment.
Attendees leave with a repeatable playbook to get seen and hired. No jargon. No algorithms. Practical guidance seekers can apply immediately.

sessions.title: Price Manipulation Detection in High-Volume Time Series Data
sessions.abstract: Meaningful events in time series rarely respect fixed time buckets. A price swing can start between bars, end early, and last seconds or minutes, yet it still needs a clear, explainable window for investigation. The challenge is scale: with 1 second sampling over a regular 6.5 hour trading session (23,400 timestamps), there are about 274 million possible start–end windows for a single instrument. Across millions of instruments, the search space grows to well over a quadrillion windows, before accounting for noise, mixed timescales, and the need to connect a move in the primary signal (price) to unusually concentrated aligned activity (participation/volume). This talk breaks down why “dynamic event windows” are hard in real systems and how to frame scalable, interpretable detection. The ideas generalize to other domains like system monitoring and healthcare signals.

sessions.abstract: Digital transformation has reached a pivot: the mandate for leadership has shifted from deploying AI for efficiency to architecting for Human-Agent Symbiosis. While agentic platforms offer unprecedented scale, success hinges on moving beyond "black-box" automation toward Agentic Integrity. To bridge the gap between technical capability and societal trust, we must address three pillars: rigorous data accuracy, proactive societal education, and empathetic design. This session provides a blueprint for "Human-First" autonomy via a 3-step Strategic Framework: 1.The Integrity Engine: Engineering agents that validate data through multi-perspective reasoning to eliminate "Shadow Logic." 2.Cognitive Restoration: Leveraging platforms to absorb robotic tasks, restoring human capacity for empathy and judgment. 3.The Societal Bridge: Strategies for educating stakeholders to move from AI-anxiety to AI-fluency. This lead a transformation that scales output while empowering the human spirit.

We’ll discuss the trade‑offs that mattered most, the lessons learned, and how aligning architecture and cost strategy lead to better outcomes.
This talk is for cloud practitioners, technical leads, and anyone working in environments where engineers and finance don’t always speak the same language. This session explores how AI governance is reshaping technical roles and why engineers, researchers, and product leaders who understand responsible AI are gaining a strategic advantage. Attendees will learn how to translate responsible AI from principle to practice, how governance frameworks affect product design, and how to leverage responsible AI expertise as a career differentiator.

sessions.title: They said Yes: How to find, ask, and keep a mentor that changes your career

This panel dismantles that fear. Voices spanning career stages, mentorship styles, mentees who have had successful mentor relationships, and diverse lived identities share the full arc of the journey: finding the right person, making the ask, sustaining it, and knowing when (and how) to move on. Critically, we include the mentor's perspective because hearing what mentors actually hope to gain is the most powerful antidote to imposter syndrome.
GHC is the perfect moment for this conversation. Attendees are already surrounded by people who want to support them. This will be a Q&A heavy session for attendees to leave with real strategies. It will give them the language, the frameworks, and the permission to finally make that ask.

sessions.title: Prompt. Judge. Decide. A Workshop on Engineering Judgment with AI
sessions.abstract:

AI-generated technical proposals can look impressive: polished language, detailed designs, and confident recommendations. But producing more technical content is no longer the hard part. Knowing what to trust, challenge, and act on is.

This workshop sharpens two skills that matter most when engineers work with AI:

First, engineering judgment. You’ll practice evaluating a realistic technical proposal: identifying what matters, questioning assumptions and evidence, weighing alternatives and cost, and deciding what you would recommend.

Second, effective AI-assisted technical design. You’ll work with an AI assistant and use techniques to frame the problem clearly, provide the right context and constraints, uncover gaps, explore alternatives, challenge recommendations, and turn the output into a design you can confidently bring to your team.

You’ll leave with practical frameworks and techniques to get stronger results from AI while raising the quality of your engineering work.

From operating on three-hour sleep cycles to calming a crying newborn who cannot yet communicate, motherhood strengthened core leadership muscles every early-career technologist must build. 

This session reframes motherhood not as a career trade-off but as advanced leadership training. Through candid stories and research-backed insights on working mothers in tech, I will share 7 lessons that strengthened my product thinking and how they apply to building teams, shipping products, and leading responsibly in AI-driven environments. sessions.title: Post SaaS: Building at the Frontier of AI and Physical Systems
sessions.abstract:
The software moat is compressing, and roles that have defined the last decade of tech careers are being automated or commoditized faster than the industry can follow. The fastest-growing, highest-leverage opportunities in tech are shifting orientation: applying AI to physical systems. The industries that underpin the global economy (chips, infrastructure, power, robotics, autonomous machines) are being reshaped by AI, and they need a new kind of thinker and technologist to build what comes next.

Normal Computing sits at this frontier, building AI for silicon engineering and developing unconventional computing architectures. 

This panel brings together two leaders from Normal Computing. Faris Sbahi, co-founder and CEO, will share why the convergence of AI and physical systems represents the defining career opportunity of this generation, and how unconventional skills will be needed to meet future demand. Hanna Yip, who came to Normal from an AI and machine learning background and now leads Normal's EDA product development, will speak about what it's like to build an AI platform for chip design engineers, and developing deep domain fluency in chip design on the job.

The session will also address the honest, practical realities of what it takes to work in product and engineering at a startup that is building completely novel tools for expert users; and thriving in a culture that values intellectual curiosity and adaptability over traditional pedigree. Normal operates a forward-deployed model where engineers work on-site with customers and own outcomes end to end, and people carry more responsibility than their titles would suggest at a larger company. Normal is one of the most difficult places to work, probably in the world; but this type of frontline engineering with customers is an opportunity to learn quickly and build domain expertise in an applied AI setting. 

Attendees will leave with a clearer understanding of where the highest-leverage careers in tech are heading , concrete strategies for navigating career transitions into deep tech and semi engineering, and an honest view of what it takes to build in novel computing paradigms.

sessions.title: Antifragile Careers: What Startup Failure Taught Me About Thriving in Big Tech
sessions.abstract:

Drawing on Nassim Taleb’s concept of antifragility, this session explores how structured exposure to uncertainty—when approached thoughtfully—builds skills, judgment, and resilience that compound over time. I’ll share my experience as an immigrant working across startup and large-scale technology environments, and how navigating change and ambiguity accelerated my professional growth.

You’ll learn how to evaluate asymmetric opportunities where downside is limited, how to manage risk through “sandboxing,” and how to position nontraditional experiences as strengths in competitive hiring markets. This session is not about taking unnecessary risks—it’s about designing a career that benefits from change.

sessions.title: The Ally Audit: Are You Building Ladders or Maintaining Walls?

In this interactive workshop, you'll conduct an honest "Ally Audit" of your own leadership behaviors. Through structured self-assessment, peer dialogue, and real-world scenario analysis, you'll identify unconscious gatekeeping patterns and develop concrete strategies to shift from "earning it the hard way" to "lifting as we climb." You'll leave with a personalized action plan for inclusive leadership that breaks cycles rather than perpetuates them.

This isn't about guilt—it's about awareness, growth, and consciously choosing to be the leader you needed when you were starting out.

sessions.title: You Are the Most Qualified — Why Are You Still Invisible?
sessions.abstract:
You outperformed. You overdelivered. You exceeded every standard they set… and they raised the bar anyway. Because maybe you just got lucky. So you go back to prove that you didn't.

You don't lack confidence. You don't have impostor syndrome. You simply lack positioning.

In the AI era, output is being commoditized. What AI cannot replicate is your judgment, your perspective, the unconventional way you solve problems, your mindful approach to building relationships, and how you lead through collaboration. The leaders who will shape the future are those who have learned to make their identity their competitive edge.

This session is for the senior leader who is done proving her worth and is ready to become the obvious choice.

Firmware controls how users physically interact with your device, yet accessibility at this level is often overlooked. Together, we'll explore how Universal Design Principles (UDPs) can guide firmware requirements. Attendees will work through defining the firmware requirements for an end-to-end product. 

You will learn how integrating Universal Design Principles at the firmware level supports flexible, maintainable products that adapt to users. By the end, you will walk away with a practical, repeatable blueprint for defining firmware requirements that address accessibility early in the product development lifecycle.

Nonprofits struggle with all aspects of running an organization. The main requirement for board service is PASSION. During this workshop, participants will be inspired and activated for board service. Each segment moves participants from awareness → clarity → confidence → commitment → actionable steps. sessions.title: Scaling Stability: How to Build Resilient Human Systems
sessions.abstract:
In software engineering, resilience traditionally focuses on a system's ability to withstand component failure. This session shifts the focus to the engineer. Led by Senior Software Engineers from Pinterest and Uber, The Human Stack framework applies systems-design principles to mental health and team stability, especially during industry shocks like layoffs. It moves beyond standard "wellness tips" to build a robust engineering culture that prioritizes Innovation and Impact.

We will break down how to:
- Identify Single Points of Failure: Recognize high-stress burdens from siloed institutional knowledge
- Implement "Human Failovers": Build peer-support networks and documentation to allow engineers to step back without system collapse
- Monitor "Mental Latency": Use engineering metrics to detect and prevent burnout

Attendees will gain a technical mental model for resilience, ensuring the most critical part of the tech stack (the people) remains high-impact in a volatile environment.

This talk is not a FAANG fairy tale. It is the honest, specific playbook behind that two-month window: how I got professors to actually read my emails, how I reframed my AI and data science projects to be impossible to ignore, and how I cracked the on-campus job system that most international students do not even know exists. If you are doing everything right and still hearing nothing back, this talk is for you.

In today’s dynamic landscape of technology and business, effective performance is driven not solely by intellectual capability, but also by personal energy, sense of purpose, and genuine sense of belonging. This session presents wellbeing as a key aspect of organizational culture and a strategic asset, rather than just an employee benefit. The session explores how organizations can move from burnout to renewed energy by managing energy over time. 

The session highlights how bottom up wellbeing culture drives inclusion, retention, and high performance. Participants will reflect on what it means to reset, recharge, and refocus in the midst of fast-paced AI-powered work environment, and how everyday practices such as movement, breathwork, and mindfulness can strengthen focus, resilience, and decision making. 

At Grace Hopper Celebration, Asti and Rakhi strive to bring a powerful message: when wellbeing and inclusion come together, diverse technologists can stay bold, resilient, and ready to lead.

The transition from software developer to engineering manager isn’t just a promotion - it’s a career change. After years of debugging code, you're suddenly "debugging" human dynamics, cross-team influence and emotional intelligence, often with zero documentation.

As a female engineer turned leader in a male-dominated field, I’ll share how I redefined technical credibility beyond coding, embraced the emotional complexity of leadership and learned that management is a balancing act: leading down, collaborating across & managing up.

In this session, I’ll share lessons from my transition from developer to engineering manager, including the mindset shifts and practical frameworks that helped me move from individual contributor to team multiplier.

Through candid stories and practical frameworks, you'll leave with a "README.md" for engineering managers, to stay technically strong, measure success beyond personal output and lead the human side of engineering no CS degree prepares you for.

They have proven demand, secured funding, and are growing rapidly, but they have not yet built the full structure that enables a large company to thrive. This stage gives early career professionals unique opportunities to design processes, influence cross functional systems, and expand scope faster than in enterprises.

This session will show why scale ups are one of the fastest ways to accelerate your career and how to spot them when evaluating your next move.

Voice AI has evolved from rigid scripts to systems that take real actions. In production, automation shapes trust and financial outcomes.

We'll share how we built voice AI that resolves routine issues while bringing humans in when empathy and judgment matter. You'll see our technical decisions: evaluating capabilities against experience needs, balancing performance with quality, solving for real-world noise and interruptions, and progressing to agentic AI that moves beyond scripts.

We'll explore patterns from production: confidence thresholds triggering escalation, guardrails preventing poor experiences, interruption-friendly design, and agent copilot reducing handle time while preserving empathy. You'll see what makes handoffs seamless versus frustrating. Applicable across industries where voice meets critical moments, you'll leave with a blueprint for launching voice AI that customers, agents, and leaders trust.

Closing the gap requires knowing where to bet, what to build, and how to scale.​

Three women own these three critical layers of PayPal's AI stack serving hundreds of millions of users. Uma Kona makes the strategic bets: which to take, when to invest, and how to build a strategy that holds up when AI capabilities are evolving fast. Linsey Pang builds native AI solutions from scratch, fine-tuning models on decades of proprietary data no competitor has. Connie Miao leverages research and strategy to build innovative agentic AI products, creating the consumer experiences that PayPal users rely on every day. This panel is no hype, no theory. sessions.title: AI as a Decision Layer: Redefining Trust, Risk, and Competitive Advantage
sessions.abstract:
As enterprises accelerate digital transformation, traditional security and access models built on static rules and one time decisions are increasingly misaligned with real world risk. This session explores how AI can evolve from a tactical analytics tool into a strategic decision layer that continuously governs trust, access, and risk across the enterprise.

Designed for senior leaders and executives, the talk examines how adaptive, behavior based AI systems enable organizations to reduce risk, improve operational resilience, and build durable competitive advantage without sacrificing stability, explainability, or governance. Attendees will gain a practical framework for evaluating AI driven transformation, understanding its business impact, and avoiding common failure modes as automation scales.

sessions.title: From Cloud Native to Multi-Cloud Native: Write Once, Deploy Anywhere
sessions.abstract:
While "Cloud Native" promised portability, that promise often stops at a single infrastructure. The traditional definition rarely addresses multi-cloud realities, leaving enterprises tethered to vendors through fragmented SDKs and proprietary APIs. We must evolve to Multi-Cloud Native, a paradigm where applications are provider-agnostic from day one.

In this session, I explore architectural principles for portable applications using driver-based design patterns. I will demonstrate implementation through MultiCloudJ (Salesforce’s open-source Java SDK) and Go Cloud (Google’s library), which decouple business logic from provider code to enable true "write once, deploy anywhere" capability.

Drawing from Salesforce’s journey across AWS, GCP, and Alibaba Cloud, I share the engineering challenges of this shift. Finally, we examine how AI Native development can automate refactoring legacy code into multi-cloud native standards.

sessions.title: Gotta Cache 'Em All: Cache-Aware Coding for Real-World Performance Gains
sessions.abstract:
A 10x performance improvement by changing two lines of code? This happened in our production system!

We share a real performance issue that surprised experienced teams. The root cause? A gap in understanding how modern hardware actually runs programs. Many processors rely on built-in CPU caches, yet the way code interacts with them is rarely taught.

Why does this matter, even if performance isn't your primary focus? These blind spots appear in data pipelines, backend services, and everyday application code, quietly affecting latency and cloud costs. Understanding cache behavior provides a powerful advantage when diagnosing bottlenecks and scaling systems.

Through concrete examples, attendees learn how to harness these caches using memory layout, data access patterns, and iteration order. Practical, language-agnostic techniques are presented, with guidance to avoid micro-optimization.
Designed for early to mid-career technologists, with insights for anyone building production systems.

sessions.title: Letting Go of the Keyboard: Lessons from the Move to People Leadership
sessions.abstract:
One day you’re the go-to individual contributor. The next, you’re the people leader others look to for clarity, momentum, and confidence. That shift is often called a promotion, but it’s really a reinvention: you move from doing the work to leading the people who do it. Your technical expertise still matters, but it shows up differently through guidance, decision making, and enabling others instead of direct execution. The work becomes less tangible, ambiguity increases, and impact is measured in months rather than moments.

In this talk, we share lessons from two perspectives: a leader wrapping up their first year managing people and a seasoned leader reflecting on that same transition. We’ll dig into operating without constant validation, adjusting to delayed and indirect feedback, finding fulfillment in others’ success, and building relationships as the primary lever for trust.

sessions.title: The Friction Between Us: Leading Across Roles in Tech Transformation
sessions.abstract:
Why do smart, experienced teams still struggle during transformation? It’s rarely a lack of talent. It’s misalignment, and often it’s invisible. When we don’t understand each other’s constraints, we mistake behavior for resistance or incompetence. What looks like pushback is often someone doing exactly what their role requires.

In this panel, senior leaders from across the org unpack the incentives driving cross-role friction. They surface real tensions and model how to navigate them constructively. You’ll learn to recognize friction early, approach disagreement with curiosity instead of frustration, and assume good intentions — seeing colleagues as capable professionals operating under real constraints, not obstacles.

This isn’t about “better communication.” It’s about building the cross-role instincts that define influential leaders. Because leadership isn’t about having the answer; it’s about understanding the system.

sessions.title: Architecting a Career: Staying Technical in a Rapidly Changing World
sessions.abstract:
You finally carve out time to start that cloud certification or GenAI course. The first night goes well —then deadlines and life take over, and two weeks later you’re restarting the same module again. With GenAI acceleration, technical skills don’t stay fresh for long, and keeping up suddenly feels urgent.
This is not a time‑management lecture or a learning‑path walkthrough. It’s a practical operating model for staying technical in a rapidly shifting industry. You’ll learn the 3C Framework—Consistent, Contextual, and Connected—and apply a 90‑day Learning Roadmap to uncover hidden time pockets, choose one high‑impact skill, and design a micro‑learning habit tied to real work. You’ll learn how to embed learning into everyday workflows, build credibility through steady curiosity, and let go of the do it all mindset.
Walk away with a personalized plan, a 30‑day commitment, and curated less than 20‑minute resources you can sustain.

sessions.title: Louder Isn't Better: Making Space for the Quietly Exceptional
sessions.abstract: In most workplaces, success is measured not just by what you accomplish, but by how loudly you show up. Assertiveness and constant visibility have become the unspoken prerequisites for promotion. This bias toward extroversion undervalues the many strengths introverts bring to the table and forces them to adopt extroverted qualities just to feel secure in their roles. This talk challenges the "extrovert ideal" that quietly shapes who gets ahead, who gets heard, and who gets left behind. Attendees will walk away with practical strategies to build inclusive environments where all employees can do their best work. Ultimately, you'll feel empowered to foster a workplace culture where every voice is valued, because the quietest people in the room may have the most to offer.

sessions.title: Agent-Driven Development: Architecting Autonomous Workflows for the Modern SDLC
sessions.abstract:
AI has transformed how we write code but our operational overhead - manual Jira grooming, triaging security vulnerabilities, and regression testing - remains a bottleneck. To achieve maximum benefit,we must move beyond "chatbots (prompting) toward Agent-Driven Development (ADD): a framework for orchestrating autonomous, self-healing workflows across the SDLC.

In this session, we will deep-dive into the architecture of "Agentic Loops" that handle the heavy lifting of modern engineering. We will explore three real-world case studies:

The Project Pilot: Automating Jira backlog refinement and requirement mapping.

The Security Shield: Intelligent vulnerability triaging and automated remediation suggestions.

The Quality Loop: AI-driven Test Generation that evolves with your codebase.

Attendees will leave with a technical blueprint for selecting the right orchestration hooks, ensuring data privacy, and implementing "human-in-the-loop" checkpoints to scale AI-augmented operations with confidence

sessions.title: Find Roles Hidden in Your Skills using Graphs
sessions.abstract:
You have more career options than your job title suggests, and a graph can prove it. 

This hands-on workshop uses a career skills graph to answer the question: what roles could I move into based on what I already know how to do? Participants will explore a dataset connecting skills, job roles, and open positions, then personalize it with their own experience. 

Graphs are great at multi-hop traversal, revealing roles two or three connections away. We’ll enhance this with vector similarity to uncover semantically related skills, and an LLM layer to explain why a role fits and highlight skill gaps. 

You’ll leave with a visualized career graph and real queries to guide your next move. Who knows? You might discover an unexpected path.

sessions.abstract:
As early-career software engineers who began in Bank of America’s Global Technology Analyst Program, we quickly realized technical skill alone doesn’t create impact. The real challenge is translating business needs into scalable solutions while building confidence and credibility. In this session, we’ll share lessons on bridging business and technology early in our careers: asking strategic questions, identifying the core problem behind requests, and communicating clearly with nontechnical partners.

We’ll highlight common pitfalls, effective collaboration strategies, and practical ways early developers can influence decisions and grow professionally. We’ll also discuss how we use AI to strengthen problem-solving, improve efficiency, and accelerate learning. Finally, we’ll share leadership experiences beyond our core roles, mentorship, community involvement, and internal initiatives, that expanded our networks and shaped our long-term paths.

sessions.title: Analytics Data vs AI Data: Why your Architecture Must Evolve
sessions.abstract:
For years, data teams have optimized ETL and ELT pipelines to power dashboards, deliver trusted metrics, and drive executive decision-making. We’ve built reliable analytics foundations designed around aggregation, reporting, and customization.

But AI changes the equation.

Data built for dashboards is not the same as data built for AI-driven analytics. AI systems require richer context, stronger governance, tighter lineage, and greater reproducibility. Pipelines that work for BI often break silently when used to power models.

In this session, I’ll explore the architectural shift required to move from traditional analytics to AI-ready data platforms. I’ll share lessons from working with data leaders navigating this shift, along with practical frameworks for managing this transition and building AI systems that are not only powerful but also trustworthy.

sessions.title: Can LLM Run On-Call? Inside LinkedIn’s Autonomous Network Agent
sessions.abstract:
On-call is unforgiving. Systems fail at 2AM, not in controlled demos. At LinkedIn, we’re building the Network On-Call Agent: an autonomous AI system that moves beyond triage to real incident remediation. The agent consumes live incident events, correlates signals across dozens of infrastructure systems, dynamically loads operational knowledge, and executes controlled remediation actions, all within strict safety guardrails and audit boundaries.

This session explores what it takes to safely let AI operate in critical production environments. 

We’ll dive into event-driven workflows, validation layers, staged autonomy, cost observability, rollback strategies, and human override mechanisms. If you’re building agentic systems that must diagnose, decide, and act, without compromising reliability, this talk will show what production-grade autonomy actually requires.

sessions.title: Stop Applying, Start Building: How Non-Technical PMs Use AI Side Projects to Get Hired
sessions.abstract:
The PM job market has changed. Hundreds of applicants per role, AI screening resumes, and hiring managers who can’t tell candidates apart. For non-technical PMs, the challenge is harder: how do you prove you can ship when your resume says “strategy” but not “code”?

This panel brings together PMs who stopped waiting and started building. Each panelist has used free AI tools to ship real side projects — from voice-to-task apps to automated workflows — without writing code. These projects became the differentiator that landed interviews and offers.

Attendees will walk away with: 
- A framework for turning daily annoyances into portfolio-worthy AI projects 
- Strategies for showcasing side projects in resumes, interviews, and LinkedIn
- Honest conversation about imposter syndrome and the mindset shift from “I’m not technical enough” to “I shipped this”
For every PM, career switcher, and woman in tech told she doesn’t have the right background, and ready to prove otherwise.

sessions.title: AI and the 2026 Threatscape: Securing Innovation in the Age of Intelligent Adversaries
sessions.abstract:
As AI rapidly transforms the cybersecurity landscape, defenders are now facing intelligent adversaries capable of learning, adapting, and scaling attacks faster than traditional controls can respond. This session provides a technical, forward-looking exploration of the 2026 threatscape through real demonstrations, emerging research, and actionable frameworks.

We begin with a concise recap of 2025’s most significant attack trends from AI-generated phishing to identity-driven compromises before previewing the next wave of AI-powered reconnaissance, deepfake-enabled social engineering, and cloud-native exploitation. 

Participants will also see how AI can strengthen defense through behavior-based anomaly detection, data-centric security. 

We conclude with a practical four-step AI Security Readiness Roadmap Assess, Detect, Respond, Validate plus a resource toolkit enabling attendees to replicate the workflows in their own environments.

sessions.title: Quantum Unbound: Defeating 'Harvest Now, Decrypt Later' with Post-Quantum Cryptography
sessions.abstract:
The "Quantum Threat" is a present-day risk requiring an unbound approach to cybersecurity. Adversaries currently use "Harvest Now, Decrypt Later" (HNDL) tactics to steal encrypted data today for future decryption once quantum computers mature. We walk you through the technical transition from classical RSA and Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC) to the new era of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).

We demonstrate building "Quantum-Ready" infrastructure using the latest NIST-standardized algorithms. We teach you to implement "Crypto-Agility"—the ability to switch cryptographic standards without replacing hardware or causing downtime. We provide a technical migration blueprint for unpatchable legacy systems and brittle firmware. Join us to learn how to future-proof your organization so that your technology remains resilient against the most powerful computers ever built.

sessions.title: The Visibility Gap: Why Talent Alone Won’t Get You Promoted
sessions.abstract:
You can be exceptional at what you do and still be overlooked.

In high-growth organizations, advancement is not determined by output alone. It is shaped by visibility, narrative control, and perceived influence. The professionals who rise fastest are not always the most technically capable; they are the most clearly positioned.

At senior levels, excellence is assumed, but influence must be demonstrated.

Through candid storytelling and tactical examples drawn from both corporate leadership and the creator economy, this session will unpack why visibility is a strategic leadership skill and how to intentionally build it. Attendees will leave with practical tools to clarify their personal brand, communicate impact in high-noise environments, and position themselves for executive advancement.

sessions.title: Breaking Barriers: Thriving as the Only Woman in the Room
sessions.abstract:
For much of my life, I’ve often been the only woman in the room — in classrooms, boardrooms, and countless meetings. Over time, it became so familiar that I barely noticed it. But through conversations with other women, I realized that this experience can feel intimidating, isolating, and even discouraging. Too many talented women hesitate to chase opportunities simply to avoid standing out alone.
In this session, I’ll share a personal perspective on why being the only woman in the room doesn’t have to hold us back — and how it can become a source of strength. We’ll explore practical ways to reframe the experience, step into visibility with confidence, and create space for more women to join us in every room we enter.

This also allows an opportunity to ensure fulfillment in your work even if it doesn’t fit the typical career path.

In this session, I will discuss how women in tech can navigate career changes as "strategic migrations" to better-aligned roles, which is something I recently went through myself when switching to a Chief of Staff role in a product organization after 18+ years in tech roles. I will challenge the audience to move away from the stigma of career changes and build their own definition of success around prioritizing fulfillment, skill acquisition, and values-based development.

sessions.abstract: Product analysts often sit at the center of critical decisions — without owning an actual product roadmap. This workshop focuses on how to use metrics as a lever for influence at both the executive and team level, and how to show up as a strategic partner rather than just a reporting function. Drawing on real experience leading cross-functional initiatives — from major strategic programs anchored in one or two critical metrics to building unified, reliable data foundations — I’ll share practical techniques for framing analyses in terms leaders care about, designing metrics that clarify trade-offs, and turning “data requests” into strategic proposals. The session will include guided exercises where attendees reframe a vague ask, outline a metrics narrative for a high-stakes decision, and map the stakeholders for their next project. We’ll also talk about influencing executive stakeholders, managing interrupts versus long-term programs, and protecting time for high-impact work. Attendees will leave with concrete scripts, templates, and confidence to lead through data and operate as a strategic partner in any role.

sessions.title: Human-in-the-Loop: A Cross-Generational Approach to Responsible Health AI
sessions.abstract:
17 years ago, at GHC2009 in Tucson, when I presented Network Security research, leveraging early ML to secure networks, my toddler daughter was in the conference childcare. Today, she is a medical student at UNISR(Milan), navigating a healthcare landscape reshaped by Large Language Models (LLMs). We return to GHC to show that the bridge between code and care is built by those who understand both the algorithm and the anatomy.This session bridges two generations to address the "Translation Gap" between algorithmic output and clinical safety.

Utilizing Kahoot and Mentimeter for interactive exercises, we analyze three high-stakes ethical pitfalls, which are hallucinated histories, encoded bias, and oversight erosion. 
By merging technical rigor with clinical intuition, we propose a "Responsible AI" framework that prioritizes the patient over the prompt.

Attendees will learn to design Human-in-the-Loop systems, ensuring AI remains a clinical assistant, not a liability.

In Microsoft's Azure Compute organization, we co-led a reverse mentorship pilot where a diverse group of early-career mentors coached senior leaders (mentees) by tackling real, high-level organizational challenges the leaders brought in. That flipped mentorship model became a repeatable "career mobility engine": it rapidly builds mentors' networks and turns their fresh perspectives into credibility, while delivering tangible outcomes that hiring managers recognize and value. In this talk, we share the exact operating model we used: how we designed the program like a product, and how any individual can leverage it to gain visibility, craft a stronger career narrative, and accelerate their own career transitions.

This session blends research, tactical hiring shifts, and honest lessons learned. Attendees will leave with actionable frameworks to influence hiring decisions, cultivate sponsorship, and build diverse teams, even in traditionally underrepresented technical fields.

sessions.title: Bridging Bytes and Biology: Automating 3D Anthropological Topography
sessions.abstract: In physical anthropology and evolutionary biology, researchers rely on tedious, manual methods to measure tooth wear, leading to imperfect data and massive time sinks. Other times, they rely on expensive, fancy software. To solve this industry bottleneck, our team of four computer scientists developed "Topo Tooth," a production-ready web application that automates complex 3D topographical measurements. Built with Svelte and Threlte, this tool transforms raw CSV point clouds into interactive 3D meshes using Delaunay triangulation. By implementing radius-based spatial search algorithms, the software automatically identifies anatomical extrema (cusps and fossae) and calculates precise vectors, heights, and wear slopes. In this session, we will explore the architecture behind Topo Tooth, detail how we translated spatial mathematics into an interactive 3D UI, and share strategies for modernizing traditional scientific research.

sessions.title: Objection! The Algorithm Is Biased: The Woman-in-the-Loop Imperative
sessions.abstract:
The AI got it wrong. A woman in the room caught it. That's not a coincidence.
AI systems are making decisions that affect hiring, healthcare, safety, and opportunity and most of them were built, tested, and validated without women in the room. The result isn't always intentional bias. It's invisible bias. And the people most likely to catch it are the ones it affects. This panel is about one thing: women need to be in the room when AI decisions get made. Not as an afterthought. Not as a diversity checkbox. As the essential voice that determines whether an AI system is fair, contextual, and trustworthy. We'll hear from women who've been that voice, who've changed what systems did, who it served,. They'll challenge the idea that "human-in-the-loop" is a technical safeguard. It's a leadership role. And it demands exactly the skills imposter syndrome has been quietly convincing women they don't have: empathy, context, ethics, and the courage to say "wait, is this right?"

We'll debate the real questions mid-career technologists face: IC track vs. Management? How do you avoid being pigeonholed? How do you negotiate compensation internally? You'll leave with concrete playbooks: how to use tenure as a trust signal for high-risk roles, how to make your reputation portable across teams, and how to turn institutional knowledge into a career superpower and not a cage.

sessions.title: No Single Road to Software: The Evolution of Nontraditional Career Paths
sessions.abstract:
There has never been one “right” way to start a career in tech, and today the journeys are more varied than ever. Engineers and technical leaders increasingly are finding their pathway into the field through different industries, bootcamps, vibe coding, or career transitions. 

In this conversation, Jess Lee, co-founder of dev.to is going to be exploring how the nontraditional path into technology has evolved. Our panelists each offer a unique perspective both in and out of traditional computer science programs and will discuss how the landscape is changing.

In an era defined by rapid digital transformation, these executives will delve into how audacious goals and forward-thinking strategies are not just aspirational but are actively shaping the technological landscape. The discussion will illuminate the "art of the possible," showcasing how a mindset of limitless ambition empowers organizations to overcome challenges, drive unprecedented innovation, and redefine what's achievable in IT. A key focus of the session will be the transformative role of women in technology. The panelists will share insights on how diverse perspectives, particularly those brought by female leaders, are crucial in not only fostering a more inclusive tech industry but also in redefining its future trajectory. They will discuss how women are actively breaking down traditional barriers, challenging the status quo, and bringing unique approaches to leadership and innovation that are essential for navigating the complexities of the digital age and creating a more equitable and dynamic technological future.

sessions.title: Decisions, Not Diagrams: How Senior Engineers Shape System Architecture
sessions.abstract:
Architecture discussions often center on diagrams, frameworks, and patterns—but the systems that endure are shaped by the decisions engineers make long before any diagram is finalized.

This session explores how senior engineers navigate high-stakes architecture decisions in real-world systems—where requirements evolve, constraints shift, and there is rarely a single “correct” answer. Instead of focusing on idealized architectures, we’ll dive into the decision-making process itself: how experienced engineers frame ambiguous problems, evaluate tradeoffs, prioritize short-term needs against long-term impact, and recognize when to revisit earlier choices.

Drawing from experience building and evolving large-scale consumer systems, this session highlights decisions that scaled successfully as well as those that required course correction—and why.

Attendees will leave with practical mental models they can apply across technology stacks to make better architecture decisions when clarity is limited and the stakes are high.

Drawing on first-hand experiences with an education nonprofit in Paraguay and a First Nations social enterprise in Canada, the talk explores how assessing and recommending technology solutions within real-world constraints becomes a powerful learning experience - one that builds strategic judgment, cultural awareness, and ethical decision-making. By working in social-impact contexts beyond Silicon Valley, the talk highlights how to create meaningful impact across communities, while equipping mid-career technologists with leadership skills that translate back to enterprise and global industry settings.

sessions.title: The Human Element - Why LLMs need your Intuition
sessions.abstract:
When LLMs took the tech world by storm, many experienced developers felt a sudden, sharp sense of obsolescence. If a machine can write the code, what is left for the engineer? This session is a journey from imposter syndrome to empowerment. Through the lens of a mobile developer, I followed my natural instinct: first tinker, then dig into the roots.
By building a female-centric, cycle-synced productivity app for myself, I discovered that the most critical part of 'Prompt Engineering' isn't the mechanics—it's the human thought process behind it. Once the app was built, I went deeper into why it worked, uncovering the probabilistic nature of LLMs and how they differ from the traditional instruction sets we know. Attendees will learn how to leverage their own lived experience and foundational knowledge to steer AI outputs, moving from being a passive code-generator to an active 'Architect of Intent.'

Drawing from enterprise AI transformation experience, it outlines a modern operating model for AI-powered products centered on evaluation-first development, cross-functional governance, lifecycle orchestration for agents, and risk-aware scaling.

After interviewing hundreds of candidates at Amazon, we’ve learned this: technical skills open the door, but storytelling gets you hired. AI makes that storytelling easier—and riskier. This interactive workshop shows you how to use AI for resume optimization, interview practice, and STAR stories—while staying within ethical boundaries.

As certified interviewers, we’ve seen candidates fail by reciting AI scripts—and others succeed by using AI strategically. We’ll share insider insights and red flags that reveal inauthentic responses.

Designed for women in tech, this session tackles bias, self-advocacy, and articulating achievements with confidence. You’ll leave with practical AI tools, authentic strategies, and a 30-day action plan.

sessions.title: Beyond the Vibe Check: Evaluating Reliable AI Assistants in Production
sessions.abstract:
AI systems rarely fail with visible errors. They fail with confidence. 

A RAG assistant that worked yesterday can quietly degrade after a prompt edit, embedding update, or tool configuration change. It continues generating fluent answers. It simply stops being reliable. Without structured evaluation, these regressions are often discovered by users rather than engineers. 

Most conversations about AI evaluation focus on model benchmarks. This session focuses on production systems. We will examine how to evaluate retrieval quality, groundedness, tool-calling behavior, and regression risk in real deployments. If you are building copilots, assistants, or AI-powered features, this talk offers a systematic approach to measuring reliability before failures reach your customers.

sessions.title: Beyond Models: The 3 Pillars of Data Science

But to truly steer a company toward being data-driven, you need someone who can speak for the data, bring an analytical lens to every conversation, and hold the line between what the data shows and what the room wants it to show. It's about influencing decisions before a model is ever built, designing metrics that actually measure what matters, and making your findings land with stakeholders who never asked for them.

The session covers three pillars most Data Scientists learn the hard way: Leadership, Strategy, and Communication. Getting into the right conversations, measuring the right things, and turning analysis into decisions. sessions.title: Architecting Autonomy: How Mentorship Can Multiply Your Impact
sessions.abstract:
Mentorship shapes careers in two directions. As a mentor, you get to support someone's growth and help shape their career. As a mentee, you get to leverage someone else's experience to learn and chart your own path toward independence. Mentorship can be so powerful, but is often treated as a secondary priority instead of something built with intention. In this session, we'll explore a three phase approach to mentorship: from building trust and providing hands-on guidance, to fostering independent judgment, to creating opportunities for visibility and leadership. We'll discuss: As a mentor:

How do you support growth without creating dependency?

How do you know when advocacy accelerates growth versus undermines ownership?

How do you build a healthy support system for your mentee while juggling multiple priorities?

As a mentee:

How do you frame questions when you don't know what you don't know?

How do you decide when to ask for help versus figure it out yourself?

How do you turn feedback into action instead of just acknowledging it and moving on?

Join me as we learn what it means to architect autonomy, by supporting someone today to prepare them to thrive independently tomorrow.

sessions.title: Software Engineering to Outcome Engineering: Coding Is Dead. Engineering Isn't.
sessions.abstract: In the era of agentic programming, what does it mean to be a software engineer? Software engineering was never just about writing code, but we spent so long typing that we forgot. This session will go over how the role of a software engineer is becoming more outcome-centric. This talk introduces Outcome Engineering: why the role is shifting from producing code to defining outcomes, and how we should make that shift deliberately. We will cover why this matters now with the 99% trap (agent code that looks done but hides production-breaking flaws) and models that keep getting better at the easy part while the hard part stays human. Attendees will leave with a concrete 5 step workflow: (1) defining outcomes before touching an agent, (2) context engineering, (3) defining intent and roles, (4) doubling down on testing and risk assessment, and (5) mastering the new debugging loop. We will do some live demos, audience polling, and go over frameworks anyone can apply daily.

In this hands on workshop, we’ll introduce “Lean Action Workout,” a framework designed to help teams surface root friction, align on a shared future state, and translate that alignment into a prioritized, executable roadmap in a single session.

This approach is especially powerful for women and underrepresented leaders, who are often expected to absorb friction and “just make it work”. Rather than carrying invisible labor, this provides a structured way to create clarity that is shared, visible, and sustainable.

sessions.title: Trailblazers Show Us the Way: Women Belong in Technology
sessions.abstract: Women have led the creation of technology from the very earliest days. With women trailblazers from Ada Lovelace to Fei Fei Li and everyone in between, we can see and be inspired by their creativity and their determination to make a difference. For decades the stories of women's achievements in technology were hidden, but today there's a groundwell of effort to bring their stories to light. We draw strength from their achievements: not only are women capable of achieving innovation and discovery, but also our presence is essential, and truly the future depends on us. The right role models take us beyond showing us how to live, thru their example the principles we know in our heads take root in our hearts. With the stories of these trailblazers, we can really believe in our hearts that we belong here!

sessions.title: Architect Your Influence: How Senior ICs Drive Change Without Authority
sessions.abstract:
As a senior IC, you are responsible for outcomes across teams you don't manage, in organizations you don't control. Your power comes from influence, not authority, and that requires a completely different playbook.
Most senior ICs learn this the hard way. You write the perfect architecture proposal. You present the data. You are clearly right. And nothing happens. Because being right is not the same as being effective.
This session unpacks how senior ICs actually drive change at scale: building architectural authority, navigating cross-org politics without a title, and the counterintuitive strategies that turn "just an IC" into the person leadership turns to when direction is unclear.
You will leave with a practical influence toolkit: frameworks for RFC-driven consensus, stakeholder mapping strategies, and techniques for making your impact visible. This is not theory. This is fieldcraft.

sessions.title: AI + Human Collaboration: Redefining Roles in the AI Era
sessions.abstract:
Every generation has feared the machine. Every generation has adapted. This one is no different — except the stakes are higher, the pace is faster, and the opportunity is bigger than ever.

AI isn't coming for your job. It's coming for the parts of your job you never loved — the repetitive, the predictable, the draining. What remains is the work only you can do: the judgment calls, the ethical guardrails, the creative leaps, the human connections that no model can replicate. But thriving in this new reality isn't accidental. It requires intention.

In this session, we cut through the hype and get practical. Drawing on real-world examples across engineering, healthcare, and business operations, we'll map exactly where AI augments human capability — and where human expertise remains non-negotiable. You'll walk away with concrete frameworks for identifying where you add irreplaceable value, building the skills that matter in an AI-assisted world, and designing workflows where you direct AI rather than compete with it. Whether you're an engineer, analyst, product manager, or quality assurance professional — this session is your strategic playbook for the AI era. Not survival. Mastery.

In this panel, leaders from P33 Chicago and a Joint Venture Silicon Valley share how they design public–private partnerships (PPPs) that deliver durable regional outcomes. The conversation moves beyond success stories into the practical work: governance, accountability, data, funding, and execution, plus the tradeoffs required to move with speed without losing legitimacy.

Attendees will leave with a transferable playbook for building and governing cross-sector coalitions, concrete questions to diagnose when PPPs help (or hinder), and examples of how regions translate shared strategy into programs, talent pipelines, and investments.

This contrasts sharply with corporate "ask culture," where not asking can mean missing out on opportunities. Chaitali will share learnable skills to ask for needs across several dimensions: professional development, leadership opportunities, strategic career moves, technical upskilling, project and resource management, and work-life balance. Participants will leave with a concrete framework and a "flip-book" of asking scripts for various work situations.

sessions.title: Leadership Is Being Rewritten and Women Get to Write the Next Chapter
sessions.abstract: Leadership is evolving faster than most organizations are prepared for. AI is reshaping how work gets done, hierarchies are flattening, trust is strained, and burnout is real. Grounded in executive experience, current research, and a human-centered approach, this talk explores why traditional leadership approaches are breaking down and what is emerging in their place. It highlights why women are uniquely positioned to lead in this next era by fully owning the strengths they already bring. Participants will leave with clarity on how leadership is being rewritten, practical language to articulate their leadership value with confidence, and a modern framework for leading with clarity, courage, and connection in an AI-driven world. sessions.abstract:

Grounded in neuroscience and real-world experience, this session introduces practical regulation strategies and frameworks for building sustainable workflows that work with your brain, not against it. Drawing on insights from Microsoft’s Neurodiversity Leadership team and examples of how neurodivergent users are shaping the use of AI tools like Copilot, Mashal shows how understanding cognitive differences not only supports individual sustainability—but is actively driving innovation in inclusive workplace technology.

sessions.title: Navigating from Operational to Strategic: Ops Hero to Strategy Star
sessions.abstract:
Women seeking to transition from operational to strategic roles must proactively build their strategic portfolios and overcome the internal and generic perceptions. 

This involves:
1. Seeking Diverse Experiences: Taking positions that build diverse but transferable skill sets, especially early in careers. Women should focus on roles that provide exposure to revenue generation, business development, and profit-and-loss responsibility. 

2. Strategic Career Planning: Developing a comprehensive strategy that includes clear objectives, timeline development, and risk assessment. This plan should specifically target strategic roles and the competencies required for them. Craft a "Pivot Plan" with timelines, risks, and AI-governance competencies.

3. Visibility and Recognition: Actively promoting achievements and contributions within the organization through presentations, speaking engagements, and leadership roles. must articulate their value proposition clearly and confidently.

sessions.title: Breaking Into Tech with a Liberal Arts Degree
sessions.abstract:
Every year, early-career professionals with liberal arts degrees are told the same thing: “If you want to work in tech, learn to code.” It’s incomplete advice — and often the wrong advice. After managing eight job families and conducting more than 350 interviews at Amazon, we’ve seen how hiring decisions are actually made. Technical pedigree is rarely the deciding factor. Clear evidence of impact, structured thinking, and business value are.

Liberal arts graduates are not underqualified. They are often mispositioned. This session is a tactical, no-fluff playbook for early-career professionals who want to break into tech without apologizing for their background or overcorrecting with unnecessary credentials.

You’ll leave knowing exactly:
• What hiring managers actually look for
• How to translate your degree into competitive positioning
• Which skills to build (and which you can ignore)
• How to establish credibility in your first technical role

sessions.title: Nutritious vs. Delicious: A Health Check for AI Model Content
sessions.abstract:
Our AI children are picking up lollipops off the floor, and this session is all about teaching you when and how to say "Don't lick that!" 

In more detail, this session is about work our team has done to identify when a website, or any tokenized dataset, may be polluted, or detrimental to the quality of popular open-weight LLMs. We begin with all the background you need to understand the problem, including how modern agentic LLM updating differs from traditional ML updates. We then will have an audience participation round, where we let the audience test whether or not they can easily identify pages that are helpful (Nutritious) or harmful (Delicious) for a model to train on. Next, we discuss our original research into three techniques to automatically determine the nutritiousness of a webpage before it is crawled. Finally, we conclude with a recap and takeaways, leaving the audience with a much better understanding of what AI model pollution is and how to fix it.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: AI Raised the Bar: Redefining Job-Readiness for Entry-Level Engineers
sessions.abstract:

In the past, junior engineers were expected to write boilerplate code, build CRUD APIs, and complete small feature tickets. Today, AI can generate much of that instantly. So what does “job-ready” mean now?

This session explores how AI is reshaping expectations for early-career engineers and why traditional definitions of entry-level work are rapidly changing. Instead of competing on syntax, engineers must differentiate through systems thinking: architecture decisions, data modeling, scalability, tradeoffs, and ownership.

Attendees will learn how to use AI as a development accelerator while building deeper engineering judgment and how to position themselves competitively in a shifting hiring landscape.

sessions.abstract:

We will explore how the transition from a "survival" mindset to a "wellness" mindset is powered by the Digital Compass: AI. Drawing from experience as a Senior SRE at Microsoft, the speaker will demonstrate how to build automation that identifies patterns between Error Codes and APIs, effectively filtering out system noise.

Key Technical Deep Dives:
The Explorer Mindset: How to cultivate the psychological resilience needed for solo incident response and ‘uncharted’ system debugging.

Building the Digital Compass: Practical strategies for integrating AI (LLMs/MCP servers) into alerting logic to identify ‘errorCode + API’ patterns.

From Survival to Wellness: Using AI-driven predictive reliability to move from reactive firefighting to proactive maintenance.

This is the "Messy Middle" - the high-stakes challenge of evolving a product that is already in flight.
In the AI era, this challenge has intensified. How do you integrate probabilistic AI features into a deterministic legacy platform? How do you navigate the "mess" of iterating on a product you didn't start, while the technology itself is shifting beneath you? This session provides a survival guide for the "Builders" - the PMs, engineers, and designers who thrive in the complexity of 1 to N. sessions.title: Across the Great Divide: Lessons Learned from Storage and GPU Engineering
sessions.abstract:
For most of my career in data infra at AWS Lakehouse, I understood how petabytes of enterprise data was stored and optimized. What I did not understand was what happened to it after it left my system. The GPUs consuming with it were a black box, and for a long time I did not think it mattered.

It turned out it DID matter.

When I moved to Crusoe to build GPU observability tooling, I began seeing training jobs from the other side. A pattern emerged: significant GPU idle time unexplained by model architecture or hardware. GPUs were waiting for data loaders to assign files at runtime. The hidden variable was the data pipeline! It remained invisible because storage engineers never saw usage traces, and compute engineers lacked the context to connect the dots.

This talk weaves two threads: a case study showing how metadata-aware loading eliminates this bottleneck and meaningfully reduces wasted compute, and a personal account of my career that spans both sides of the AI-training boundary.

sessions.title: Why Most GenAI Pilots Fail and How Leaders Make the Ones That Matter Succeed
sessions.abstract:
Organizations are launching Generative AI pilots at unprecedented speed, yet most fail to move beyond experimentation. The problem is rarely the technology & it’s how leaders decide what to prioritize, measure, and scale.

This session examines why most GenAI pilots stall or fail from a leadership and decision making perspective. Drawing on real enterprise experiences in regulated environments, it introduces a practical framework leaders use to evaluate GenAI ideas, align them to business outcomes, and decide when to stop, pivot, or scale.

Attendees will learn how successful leaders define meaningful success metrics, avoid common adoption traps, and build cross-functional alignment across product, engineering, risk, and operations. Participants will leave with actionable tools to move GenAI initiatives from pilots to sustained business impact.

sessions.title: AI Beyond English: Building Multi-Lingual AI Solutions
sessions.abstract: This talk addresses the core challenges technical teams face when dealing with non-English languages in building effective AI solutions, reinforced by real-life examples. We will outline the complexity of non-English data, from tackling non-Latin character sets and low-resource languages to the practical hurdles of transforming unstructured data (like images and audio) into usable text. We will also go into the options for different technical approaches, including topics such as the complexity of language detection and cross-language processing techniques. The session will also analyze the current role and limitations of LLMs across diverse languages. We will conclude with best practices for designing and deploying high-performance, multilingual NLP systems that deliver value for practical business use cases.

sessions.title: AI Is Changing Skills — But Not Who Gets Heard
sessions.abstract:
AI is transforming how work gets done, how skills are measured, and how careers are built. Yet while technology is evolving rapidly, the systems that determine whose expertise is trusted and who advances into leadership often remain unchanged.
Drawing on international experience in SaaS and EdTech, alongside qualitative and quantitative research on workplace equity across Europe and the US, this session examines a growing disconnect in the future of work: AI may be changing what we value, but not who gets heard. Women and underrepresented professionals are frequently evaluated through outdated signals of confidence, authority, and “fit,” even as organizations claim to be future-ready.
This talk challenges audiences to rethink how leadership and talent are recognized in an AI-driven world. It offers a practical lens for redesigning evaluation, influence, and decision-making systems so that innovation reflects not just technological progress, but human progress as well.

sessions.title: Aspire to Inspire: Turning Rejection into Ripple Impact and Becoming the Leader You Once Needed
sessions.abstract: Breaking into tech isn’t just about landing the job, it’s about becoming someone who lifts others along the way. After facing countless rejections, final-round losses at top companies, and navigating the U.S. tech ecosystem as an international student, I stopped chasing “success” and started building something bigger: impact. From wearing multiple hats at a high-growth startup to mentoring students, leading Women in Tech initiatives, and helping women navigate internships and careers, I discovered a powerful truth: Career growth multiplies when you design it to serve others. In this session, I will introduce the "Aspire-Build-Give-Multiply" framework, a practical, repeatable approach that transforms setbacks into confidence, growth into leadership, and individual wins into community impact. Attendees won’t just leave inspired, they’ll leave with tools, habits, and systems. Because when one woman rises, she can bring ten more with her.

sessions.title: Alone Together: Building Collective Courage in a Connected, Lonely Tech World
sessions.abstract:
In an era where technology connects us in unprecedented ways, the loneliness epidemic persists, especially in demanding tech cultures where leaders are expected to perform alone.

This session reframes that tension as a design and leadership problem, not a personal failure. Drawing on lessons from high‑stakes environments — extreme mountain expeditions and global legal systems — Anjali Mehta explores collective courage as a measurable leadership practice that leads to inclusive innovation and meaningful systems change.

We go through: actionable frameworks to build psychological safety and trust across teams; leadership practices that turn vulnerability into sustainable, innovative performance; strategies for embedding collective courage into team norms, increasing innovation and opportunity for systems change. 

Attendees will leave with tools they can apply immediately to strengthen connection, influence, and effectiveness as leaders in tech.

sessions.title: Building Culture and Influence on Technical Teams: What I Wish I’d Known
sessions.abstract: Strong teams are shaped in small choices—how we listen, decide, and show up. This interactive session shares six lessons I wish I had learned sooner about building team culture in technical environments. Early in our careers, we’re taught to ship code and solve problems, but rarely how to intentionally shape the culture that makes those outcomes possible. Through practical, hard-earned takeaways, we’ll explore what builds trust, strengthens collaboration, and sustains performance. We’ll examine the invisible dynamics of decisions, feedback, conflict, and psychological safety. The session also highlights the often invisible work women in STEM carry, framing culture-building as leadership, not “extra” work, and empowering participants to strengthen teams while advancing their careers. Building culture isn’t accidental—it’s intentional, and it’s the leadership many of us wish we’d understood sooner.
