sessions.title: Build a success mindset
sessions.abstract:
In our fast paced and constantly disruptive workplaces- especially in this age of AI, women in technology face many #internal and #external barriers on our journey to unlock our maximum success.

These barriers can deplete us of our energy and play tricks on our mind to make us believe we are not set up for long term and sustainable success.

Using the power of AI, and small group discussions, this interactive workshop will #equip, #empower and #energize to build a success mindset from inside-out so you can remain on track to unlock your maximum success- no matter what comes your way.

Drawing from our joint lived experiences (former VP at IBM, Founder and CEO and a best selling author,  former CTO at Microsoft/Podcast host and Software Engineer at ClickUp), we'll guide you through practical exercises and discussions to:

1. Intentionally Aim High

2. Craft your Personal Success Plan

3. Show your worth in every interaction.

4. Own your Power.

5. Reflect and Celebrate weekly to remain energized.

You will learn to move towards your success on a daily basis and pivot when necessary.

sessions.title: Align Your Work With What Executive Teams Actually Care About
sessions.abstract:
Do you ever question how your work impacts the bottom line? Do you wonder, how to best communicate your impact? Many professionals work hard, yet struggle to gain visibility with leadership. Understanding how to speak the language of the C-suite is essential.

In this session, Parul Lahoti Bhandari introduces a practical framework built around five core metrics that executive teams consistently use to evaluate priorities: growth, risk, customers, efficiency, and future position. Drawing on experience across technology, operations, and customer success, she demonstrates how professionals at any level can translate their work into language that resonates with decision-makers.

Key Takeaways
- The five metrics executive teams use to guide decisions and prioritize investments
- How to translate technical or functional work into business-relevant outcomes
- Practical techniques for communicating impact 
- Strategies to increase visibility and influence regardless of role or title

sessions.title: Growing Your Career While Working with Legacy Systems
sessions.abstract:
Legacy code is inevitable in long-standing and high-impact systems. Early-career engineers are often told to avoid legacy systems, as they’re frequently perceived as confusing, built on outdated practices, or detrimental to system reliability. However, they are missing a key opportunity for technical and professional growth, as working with legacy systems builds skills like deep product and domain expertise, effective stakeholder communication, and cross-functional collaboration.
In this workshop, participants will explore how all long-standing systems gradually become “legacy,” and how modern engineers can evolve legacy code without breaking what works. Through hands-on activities inspired by real-world financial systems, participants will practice evaluating trade-offs with stakeholders and be introduced to modern technologies.
By the end of this session, participants will look at legacy code as a source of learning and opportunity, rather than a liability.

AI coding tools are transforming how engineers build software. They can generate code, write tests, and suggest solutions in seconds. But are we becoming smarter engineers — or just faster ones?This session explores the difference between over-relying on AI and using it strategically. Through relatable examples, we’ll discuss how AI can either strengthen critical thinking or gradually weaken problem-solving skills.

Designed for engineers at all levels, this talk focuses on maintaining strong fundamentals, sound judgment, and technical confidence in an AI-driven world. Attendees will leave with practical strategies to use AI as a thinking partner — ensuring it amplifies their skills rather than replaces them.

sessions.title: From Great to Sought-After: The Strategic Shift Women in Tech Must Make
sessions.abstract:
Many of us in tech were taught that if we work hard, stay humble, and consistently deliver excellent results, we will rise. So we do it all. We raise our hands. We stay late. We become the reliable problem-solvers and steady force behind key initiatives. Yet despite our excellence, we often find ourselves overlooked for high-visibility opportunities, excluded from strategic conversations, or passed over for leadership roles.

With two decades at Microsoft and now coaching high-performing professionals, and as author of The Sought-After Leader (June 2026), Uma Subramanian has witnessed a difficult truth: greatness builds credibility, but it does not automatically create influence or demand.

This session explores the strategic shifts required to move from excellent to sought-after. Attendees will learn how to elevate their impact from execution to strategy, strengthen their influence in critical moments, and become leaders whose contributions are actively sought, valued, and rewarded.

sessions.title: Inner Workshop: Lead the Moment by Leading Yourself
sessions.abstract:
The higher you climb, the more you're asked to hold - complex decisions, evolving team dynamics, organizational pressure, and the constant calibration of how you show up. For experienced women in tech, the challenge of leadership is not simply capability. It is capacity. And how you lead yourself - your clarity, your presence, your ability to recover - directly shapes the team, culture and performance around you.

This workshop works directly with the internal mechanisms that govern how you think, respond, and replenish - drawing on the toolkit the TLEX Institute brings to executives at leading global organizations, including evidence-based breath work and meditation as precision instruments for cognitive performance and leadership presence.

We'll explore what it means to lead each moment from a place of genuine steadiness. When you are regulated, you think more clearly. When you are present, your team feels it. When you recover well, you lead with range. These are not soft outcomes. They are the conditions that make everything else in your leadership possible - the quality of your decisions, the trust you build, the connection you create.

This workshop is experiential and designed for inner growth that extends well beyond the room. You will leave with resources to cultivate your mind, sustain what you've built, and connect with a community navigating the same terrain.

This panel offers a behind-the-scenes look at how leaders across hyperscalers and enterprise platforms are navigating this shift. Panelists from engineering, product, technical program management, operations and consulting will share how their roles have evolved as AI moved from experimentation to business-critical infrastructure.

Together, they will explore how enterprises are adopting AI, which skills are becoming essential, and how professionals are redefining leadership and impact in an AI-native workplace. This session goes beyond hype to focus on how professionals are learning new technologies, managing uncertainty, and shaping AI adoption while delivering business value. Attendees will gain practical insights to help future-proof their careers by harnessing AI.

sessions.title: Responsible AI at Global Scale: Governance, Compliance, and Contextualization
sessions.abstract:
An AI model ships globally overnight. It sounds fluent, but offends culturally in one market, breaks layout in another, misformats currency elsewhere, and violates a disclosure rule in a fourth. The model is accurate. The business is at risk.

This is the cost of scaling AI without scaling governance.

At PayPal, operating across hundreds of regulatory regimes has required building compliance, linguistic intelligence, and market validation directly into our platforms. In the AI era, reactive reviews are not enough. Regulatory fragmentation, design variability across languages, and market-specific financial laws demand governance-by-design.

In this session, I’ll share how to embed regulatory intelligence, locale-aware validation, and policy enforcement into AI architectures, separating model capability from compliance control. Responsible AI at global scale is not just about ethics; it is about operationalizing trust in real time.

sessions.title: Autonomous Incident Response with AWS DevOps Agent
sessions.abstract:
Cloud engineering teams are drowning in incidents. Manual troubleshooting, endless logs, and pressure to resolve issues quickly make incident response exhausting — driving talented people, disproportionately women, out of the field.

  Autonomous agents are changing that. By investigating incidents like an experienced DevOps engineer — correlating signals across your observability tools, runbooks, and code automatically — AWS DevOps Agent transforms operational response and makes cloud engineering sustainable.

  In this hands-on workshop, we walk you through creating and configuring Agent Spaces and investigating real incidents across EC2 and Lambda workloads. You'll see how autonomous agents detect failures, correlate signals, identify root causes, and deliver actionable mitigation plans — then help prevent future incidents — without starting from scratch at 2am.

  You'll leave with practical experience setting up and using autonomous agents for incident response, and an understanding of how this technology reduces operational burden and makes cloud engineering more accessible and sustainable.

Laptop required — this is a hands-on session, so please bring your own laptop.

sessions.title: Build Your Career Before You're Hired: Digital Presence in the AI Era
sessions.abstract:
Early-career professionals are entering a job market shaped by rapid technological change and increasing uncertainty. Traditional career paths are less predictable, and resumes alone are no longer enough to stand out. Today, digital presence plays a critical role in creating visibility, credibility, and opportunity.

In this session, Martina Matthews shares lessons from joining the founding team of Chegg immediately after college and building a career by saying yes to opportunities before feeling fully qualified. She will introduce a practical framework for building a strong digital presence using tools such as LinkedIn, AI assistants, and Canva.

Attendees will learn how to position themselves online, communicate their strengths clearly, and use AI to accelerate career growth. Participants will leave with a simple, actionable plan for building a professional presence that creates opportunity early in their careers.

sessions.title: Data Foundations for Agentic AI - Vision to Value
sessions.abstract:
Agentic AI marks a strategic shift—from tools to teammates that can reason, decide, and execute in pursuit of business outcomes. For executives, the question is no longer if agents will transform the enterprise, but how to build the right data foundation to unlock value—quickly and responsibly.

This session will present a forward-looking vision for the data foundations that enable enterprise-grade agentic AI to move from ambition to impact. We will explore how to federate data architectures for real-time, context-aware agents; establish governance models that balance speed with trust; and cultivate a data-driven culture and operating model that accelerates innovation rather than constrains it.

Leaders will leave with practical insights on compressing time-to-value, aligning data strategy with business outcomes, and organizing teams to responsibly scale AI agents as trusted digital teammates across the enterprise.

sessions.title: Uncertainty is a Feature, Not a Bug: Thriving Through Motherhood, Mortgages and Career Plateaus
sessions.abstract:
Do you feel like your career algorithm is stuck in an infinite loop? We're told growth requires "hustle," but what happens when life throws exceptions you can’t catch—like visa renewal anxiety, a heavy mortgage, the identity shift of motherhood, or a career plateau?
In this session, we'll reframe these constraints not as system failures, but as features forcing clarity. Inspired by the "10x is easier than 2x" philosophy, we will explore how limitations help strip away the non-essential. When your bandwidth is capped by paperwork, finances, or a toddler, you lose the luxury of "busy work." You're forced to identify the few high-impact actions that actually move the needle.
You'll leave with a framework for setting goals when the future feels foggy. We'll ditch rigid 5-year plans for a "micro-commit" strategy – taking small, non-threatening steps that compound into massive results. Stop waiting for perfect conditions and start shaping your path forward, right where you are

This panel brings together five first‑generation Latinas from immigrant households, all former tech interns and now professionals at Microsoft: two software engineers, two product managers, and a product marketing manager. Each broke barriers their families never imagined, whether becoming the first to attend college, enter tech, or work in the U.S. 

This is a safe, honest space to talk about the real cost of being the first: what it takes to break into tech, imposter syndrome, cultural pressure, financial responsibility, and the moments of doubt behind every “yes” and every offer. If you’ve ever wondered whether you belong in tech, this session shows you how to build your own seat, and hold the door open for those coming after you.

sessions.abstract:
As we pivot from simple chatbots to autonomous Agentic Workflows, the engineering challenge moves beyond "one-shot" prompting toward iterative reasoning loops. For a system to be effective, it must master four core design patterns: Reflection, Tool Use, Planning, and Multi-Agent Collaboration. However, in production-grade systems, autonomy without accountability is a liability, prompting the need for a new Trust Architecture. 
This panel draws on firsthand experience building production-grade multi-agent orchestration systems at Adobe and Intuit and explores building this architecture by combining standardized protocols like the MCP for secure tool use with Constitutional AI for ethical self-correction. We will debate the challenges of managing Human-on-the-loop systems and the disciplined evaluation processes required to ensure agents remain aligned in unpredictable environments. sessions.title: Staying Relevant When the Ground Won’t Stop Moving
sessions.abstract:
Twelve months ago, we were building elaborate agent frameworks, complex RAG stacks, and orchestration layers to compensate for model limitations. Today, frontier models are quietly absorbing much of that scaffolding. Larger context windows, stronger reasoning, and native tool use are collapsing layers of glue we once believed were essential.

The half-life of AI best practices is shrinking.

In this keynote, I reflect on what it means to lead and build in a world where last year’s architecture becomes today’s technical debt. Drawing from enterprise-scale AI deployments, I will explore the shift from heavy scaffolding to starting simple—and from building glue to designing domain-driven evaluation.

As models improve, durable advantage moves away from elaborate orchestration and toward judgment: knowing what “good” looks like, building feedback loops that sustain quality, and architecting systems that expect replacement. The system hasn’t disappeared—it has moved upward, into governance, observability, cost discipline, and human alignment.

But this is also a personal story. What does it feel like to watch carefully engineered best practices age in months? How do we maintain confidence and clarity when the technology redefines itself faster than our roadmaps? And how do we help the next generation build careers that endure beyond any single stack?

In a world where models eat the glue, the most important skill is not mastering today’s infrastructure—it is learning how to evolve with it.

sessions.title: Behind the Magic: GitLab Disaster Recovery
sessions.abstract:

This session shares how the WDI SRE Core Team engineered a production-ready disaster recovery strategy for GitLab, protecting over 2TB of critical data across hundreds of users and thousands of pipelines. Attendees will learn how immutable AWS Backup Vaults, automated backup plans, layered monitoring, and repeatable DR testing work together to ensure GitLab can be restored quickly when the unexpected happens.

Using real-world examples and live-tested recovery workflows, this talk reframes disaster recovery as part of the show design itself—because when systems fail, the magic doesn’t stop, and the curtain never has to fall.

sessions.title: Cultivating Resilience: Engineering Agriculture with Graphs and Spatial AI
sessions.abstract:
Global agriculture is no longer a collection of isolated data points—it is a connected system shaped by climate, geography, and rapidly changing conditions. Yet most data platforms still treat these dimensions independently, limiting our ability to make reliable, AI-driven decisions.

In this session, we explore how a hybrid approach—combining ontologies, knowledge graphs, and spatial intelligence—enables context-rich, decision-ready data. Through a real-world agricultural logistics scenario, we demonstrate how semantic models (RDF) establish meaning, property graphs enable high-speed connected data retrieval, and spatial analytics adds critical location awareness.

You’ll see how this “brain + muscle” architecture powers context-augmented AI, where the system performs reasoning and data retrieval before invoking the LLM—reducing hallucination and improving reliability. We’ll walk through an end-to-end workflow that transforms a complex question into a grounded, explainable recommendation.

Whether you’re designing data platforms or building AI-driven solutions, this session provides a practical blueprint for turning disconnected agricultural data into intelligent, actionable insight.

sessions.abstract:

This technical session breaks down proven patterns: ReAct (Reasoning + Acting), Chain-of-Thought, Tree-of-Thoughts, and Reflection. Learn when to use each pattern, how to compose them for complex workflows, and critical production considerations.
Drawing from enterprise experience in financial services, we'll explore multi-agent collaboration, memory systems, error handling, and evaluation frameworks. Demonstrations use LangGraph and LangChain, but architectural principles apply universally.
Whether building customer service agents, data analysis workflows, or autonomous systems, you'll gain practical patterns applicable across any stack—with code examples, architecture diagrams, and a decision framework for pattern selection.

sessions.title: From Invisible to Influential: 3 Signals That Turn Work into Recognition and Promotions
sessions.abstract:
Many women in tech consistently deliver high-quality work yet struggle to gain recognition or secure promotions. Often, the issue is not caliber but how impact is perceived, communicated, and connected to leadership signals.
In technical roles, early promotion gaps compound over time. McKinsey’s 2022 analysis found that for every 100 men promoted to manager in tech, only 52 women were promoted. Research on performance evaluations (2021–2023) shows women are more likely to receive personality-coded feedback than impact-focused language, shaping how leadership potential is assessed.
This session introduces the 3 Signals of Influence, a practical framework to counter these dynamics by making impact measurable and ownership visible.
Participants will gain a repeatable strategy to translate strong work into recognized influence and promotion momentum, even in environments shaped by bias.

Those insights shaped the evolution of STORYHabits.

sessions.title: Returnships After the Boom: A Leadership Strategy for Unlocking Overlooked Talent
sessions.abstract:
A decade ago, returnships were a niche idea found mostly on Wall Street. In 2016, tech companies began exploring these programs to tackle gender imbalances and find talent in a tight labor job market. The model scaled rapidly and major companies invested. By 2022 hundreds of programs had launched and thousands of women were hired.

Then the market shifted, hiring contracted, and many companies pulled back on talent initiatives — including returnships. 
What does that mean for women trying to return to careers in tech? And for leaders trying to hire the talent needed for the next wave of tech innovation?

Drawing on a decade of data and frontline experience building programs with 100+ companies, this session examines why returnships grew, why some stalled, and what comes next. We’ll share workforce trends, insights from leaders in tech, and practical frameworks companies of any size can use to design sustainable pathways to ensure that mid-career women remain part of tech’s future.

sessions.title: The Architecture of Inequality: Deconstructing Gender Bias in AI and the Power of Inclusive Tech
sessions.abstract:
The myth that Artificial Intelligence(AI) is inherently fair masks a dangerous reality: algorithms amplify historical gender biases. With women comprising just 12% of senior AI professionals , systems systematically default to a male-centric paradigm.

This presentation explores the profound impacts of this algorithmic patriarchy. We unpack staggering metrics: LLMs are 3 to 6 times more likely to default to rigid gender stereotypes , while computer vision systems have a 34% error rate for darker-skinned women. These biases drive systemic harm, from AI recruiters penalising older female candidates to economic models erasing women's unpaid labor.

Crucially, we reveal the massive socioeconomic dividend of fixing this architecture. Rectifying bias is a powerful lever for equity , capable of unlocking a projected 20% boost to global economic output and transforming AI from an engine of marginalization into a catalyst for true parity.

sessions.title: Leading Through the Age of AI
sessions.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming technology at an unprecedented pace, reshaping how we build products, solve problems, and interact with information. Yet while the technology itself is advancing rapidly, the organizations that succeed in the age of AI will not be defined by their models alone. They will be defined by their people, culture, adaptability, and leadership. As companies navigate one of the most significant technological shifts in decades, the challenge is no longer simply keeping up with innovation. It is building organizations that can continuously learn, evolve, and thrive amid constant change. How do leaders create environments where people embrace new technologies rather than fear them? How do teams balance speed with trust, innovation with resilience, and technical excellence with human judgment? And how do individuals build careers that remain meaningful and impactful as the nature of work evolves? Drawing on lessons from Bloomberg's own journey through multiple waves of technological transformation, this session will explore the human side of innovation—from fostering adaptable teams and inclusive cultures to empowering technologists to grow alongside the technologies they help create. We will discuss why diverse perspectives and strong leadership are essential to navigating uncertainty, and why the most successful organizations will be those that invest as deeply in people as they do in technology. For attendees at every stage of their careers, this conversation is an invitation to think beyond the tools themselves and focus on the qualities that endure. In the age of AI, lasting success will come not from technology alone, but from the people who shape what comes next.

sessions.title: Can Quantum Computers Solve Real-World Problems Yet?
sessions.abstract:
Quantum computing has the potential to reshape the world, but what can today's quantum machines actually do? This talk focuses on the problems most accessible to near-term quantum hardware, and examines where quantum approaches meaningfully apply today.

We'll explore how real-world optimization problems are mapped onto quantum systems, and take a look at current techniques such as quantum annealing, QAOA, and VQE algorithms. Using case studies across industries, we'll see how quantum optimization shows up in practice in areas like traffic routing, finance, and energy scheduling. Attendees will learn how to assess which problems fit today's quantum hardware, what the key technical limits are, and why most results rely on hybrid quantum-classical approaches.

This session is designed for technologists and strategy leaders who want a high-level understanding of what quantum computers can do in 2026, and how to make informed decisions about piloting it inside organizations.

sessions.title: From Skipping Every Opportunity to Building a Community I Wish I'd Had
sessions.abstract:
I was terrified of being a CS major. I didn't fit the typical tech stereotype, and instead of pushing through that discomfort, I let it shrink me.  I literally thought LeetCode was a programming language. I skipped opportunities, avoided putting myself out there, and stayed as invisible as possible. On paper I was in the program. In reality I was hiding.

Junior year, I decided it was time to change things for myself. I started showing up as the person I wanted to become, even before I felt ready. And slowly, everything started to shift.

After graduating, I started hosting monthly tech panels so others wouldn't feel that same isolation. But after 5+ events, I noticed a gap: students left inspired, then went right back to job searching alone. Inspiration wasn't enough. People needed structure, accountability, and someone in their corner.

That's when I built a recruiting buddy matching system from scratch, while working full time, with no team and no roadmap. What started as a workaround for a problem I personally lived became a 500-person community I wish had existed when I was starting out.

This session is for anyone who has ever felt too hidden to start.

You'll leave knowing:

- How to start showing up in rooms where you don't yet feel like you belong

- How to spot when you need accountability, not just inspiration

- How to find people who will actually help you follow through

- How to create structure that keeps you moving between the big moments

- How to build a support system without waiting for someone else to build it for you

Adoption of spatial intelligence follows a maturity curve - from no geospatial usage, to fragmented tools, to scalable platforms still limited to specialist teams. Today, AI is shifting that curve by embedding spatial context directly into decision workflows. Drawing on experience working with organizations across industries, this session explores why spatial intelligence is becoming a business essential and how AI is accelerating its impact in real-world decision-making.

Yet saying "no" can feel risky, like we may be seen as difficult, not collaborative, or not ready for the next level.

As roles grow more complex, success depends not only on technical excellence but also on emotional intelligence, communication, and the ability to influence outcomes. 

This session explores why many technical professionals hesitate to speak up, how unspoken expectations shape decisions, and how defaulting to “yes” can quietly limit career growth and lead to burnout.

Through realistic scenarios, guided reflection, and repeatable techniques, attendees will gain practical tools to set expectations, say “no” without damaging trust, and communicate with confidence in high-stakes situations, strengthening relationships and supporting continued career growth.

sessions.title: From APIs to Agents: Translating Backend Architecture into Agent Workflows
sessions.abstract:
Agentic AI can feel like an entirely new discipline. When I transitioned from backend engineering into machine learning engineering, that is exactly how it felt. The breakthrough came from recognizing that production agents are still software systems. They ingest data through APIs, move through structured workflows, route decisions, call downstream services, and manage state under failure conditions.
In this session, I translate five core backend design patterns into their agentic equivalents. Using a vendor-agnostic email triage-and-action agent that ingests customer emails, classifies intent, triggers downstream services, and generates structured responses, I demonstrate how these familiar patterns evolve when an LLM becomes part of the workflow.
Attendees leave with a five-pattern mapping framework and a practical readiness rubric they can apply directly to systems they already build, allowing them to approach agent development with the skills they already possess.

sessions.title: Start Anyway: How Unplanned Paths Lead to Cyber Careers
sessions.abstract:

This talk is for anyone who has ever felt behind, underqualified, or unsure what move to make next. It starts with a story: in high school, I was featured in the CodeGirl documentary for building an app that solved a real community problem. I had no idea that moment would eventually lead me to product security. The path from there was not straight. It went through computer science, embedded systems, and a few wrong turns before landing where I am now.

Security careers rarely follow a script. The field moves too fast, the roles are too varied, and the best practitioners usually came from somewhere unexpected. That is not a bug. That is how the industry works.

You will leave with frameworks for building skills with intent, growing influence without a title, and spotting your next move before someone hands it to you.

sessions.title: 5 Techniques to Stop AI Agent Hallucinations
sessions.abstract:
AI agents hallucinate in four distinct ways: fabricating data from approximate search, picking wrong tools, ignoring business rules, and claiming success on failed operations.

In this workshop, you'll tackle all four failure modes with production-tested techniques. Starting with Graph-RAG to replace vector search with structured knowledge graphs for precise data retrieval, then semantic tool selection using FAISS to dynamically filter dozens of tools to the most relevant per query.

Next, neurosymbolic guardrails that enforce business rules through verifiable code the LLM cannot bypass. Then, runtime steering that allows the agent to self-correct instead of blocking when it violates operational rules. Finally, multi-agent validation where specialized agents cross-check each other's work through structured debate.

Using a travel booking agent as our running example, each technique builds on the previous one. You'll leave with five reusable patterns and a decision framework for choosing which techniques to apply based on your specific hallucination challenges. Laptop with Python 3.9+ required.

sessions.title: Doing the Scary Thing First: How Engineers Can Grow at Every Level
sessions.abstract:
Regardless of where they are in their career, engineers often feel like they should wait for confidence and clarity before taking ownership. But in reality, high-impact work and growth opportunities don’t wait. These moments appear throughout an engineering career. From submitting your first PR to leading a cross-team effort, growth often shows up disguised as discomfort.
When engineers hold back instead of leaning into the unknown, they lose time, stall their career development, and miss chances to make meaningful impact.
In this workshop, attendees will reflect on their own success (of any size!) to pinpoint factors that made those wins possible. Using a third-person lens, they’ll practice coaching a friend through a tough scenario, then apply the same method to a real challenge they’re facing to map out concrete next steps. 
Attendees will leave with an actionable plan for a task they’ve been avoiding, as well as a repeatable approach for confidently taking ownership under pressure.

Attendees will leave with concrete frameworks and decision tools to move from idea to product-market fit and scale on their own terms.

sessions.title: Agentic AI for Breast Cancer Detection Using Wavelet Multi-View Learning and Spatial Transcriptomics
sessions.abstract: This presentation introduces an agentic AI framework for histopathological breast cancer detection that integrates wavelet-enhanced deep learning with spatial transcriptomic analysis. The session demonstrates how multi-scale features are extracted from whole-slide histopathology images using wavelet-enhanced convolutional neural networks, while high-dimensional gene expression data are analyzed through interpretable linear algebra techniques including Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), and Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF). An agentic decision module autonomously evaluates reconstruction error, variance preservation, and numerical stability to select optimal representations across modalities. The presentation emphasizes mathematical rigor, interpretability, and clinical relevance, illustrating how applied linear algebra and agentic reasoning can improve diagnostic precision and transparency in healthcare AI systems.

Mobile apps are evolving into intelligent, AI-powered experiences. But moving from an "AI wrapper" to a production-ready feature takes more than calling a model — it requires managing on-device inference, non-deterministic behavior, and a model that now ships with the OS itself. In this session, Divya Ravi, Senior iOS Engineer, breaks down the architecture of AI-driven iOS applications in the post-WWDC26 landscape.

We'll cover the on-device Foundation Models framework and Core ML, the real trade-offs between on-device, private-cloud, and third-party models, and the discipline that separates demos from shipping products: evaluating non-deterministic systems and securing agentic features against new risks like prompt injection. Whether you're a mid-level or senior engineer, you'll leave with a practical blueprint for building scalable, maintainable, and trustworthy AI features.

Beyond the code, Divya will share how mastering these emerging technologies can accelerate your career and position you as a technical leader in the AI era.

sessions.abstract:

I share how quality engineering and data science partnered to build an AI quality program from scratch - evolving from evaluation into red-teaming, safety guardrails, and now Disparate Impact Analysis.

I'll walk you through three layers: (1) a reproducible evaluation pipeline measuring whether AI outputs are accurate, context-grounded, and relevant; (2) adversarial red-teaming and guardrails that stress-test AI agents before release; and (3) Disparate Impact Analysis, in progress, comparing outputs across demographic groups to make fairness a permanent quality gate.

Whether you're a QA engineer, data scientist, or leader building AI accountability, you'll leave with practical templates you can use.

Whether you are looking to speed up training or architect models that are too big to train, this talk provides the blueprint for scaling without framework lock-in. Leave with the skills to implement autosharding and hybrid parallelism, ensuring your AI infrastructure is future-proof and ready for the billion-parameter era.

This youth-centered panel features current and former STEM Next Flight Crew members sharing what helped them build confidence, belonging, and momentum early in their tech career pathways. Through an open conversation moderated by a seasoned leader in tech, panelists will reflect on what supported them, what got in their way, and how they created spaces where they could see themselves thrive. Students will hear relatable stories about navigating gendered spaces in STEM and sustaining early interests into college and beyond. Attendees will leave with practical insights and encouragement for building community, finding support, and continuing their own journeys in technology.

Drawing from experience as an AWS TAM supporting startups/enterprises and contributing to Sales Accelerator premium support upsells, this session shows how women can strategically pivot into high-impact sales roles.
Tech sales is a powerful career accelerator delivering 20%+ revenue uplift from diverse teams, uncapped earnings, and executive paths in AI/cloud ecosystems. It addresses women’s hesitations (male-dominated cultures, confidence gaps, bias in promotions, rejection fears, aggressive stereotypes) by reframing sales as empowering: leverage existing technical/customer-facing skills + AI tools overcome barriers, and drive equitable growth.

sessions.title: From the Ground Up: Engineers Leading Inclusive Programs Without Formal Authority
sessions.abstract:
Mentorship, career development, and inclusion programs are most effective when built by the engineers they are meant to support. Yet, those who experience these gaps most acutely are often individual contributors without the authority, resources, or roadmap to drive change. How can early-career engineers take action and advocate for what they need without formal power?
In this panel, four engineers will share how a grassroots, engineer-led inclusion effort grew into a department-level program focused on mentorship, career growth, and community. We’ll discuss how first-hand experience surfaced real needs, how leadership emerged organically, and how structure and strategy helped these initiatives scale.
Through candid lessons on turning intent into impact, navigating leadership without authority, and avoiding burnout, this session aims to equip attendees with the tools and confidence to drive the cultural change they want to see.

sessions.title: Reclaiming Power and Resilience in the AI-Driven 'Efficiency Era’
sessions.abstract: The technology sector is undergoing a structural "Efficiency Era," with over 600,000 jobs lost in January alone and AI cited as a primary driver. For mid-career women (8–15 years), this creates a unique "double-bind": statistically more vulnerable to layoffs (1.6x more likely) while juggling disproportionate "sandwich generation" caregiving and a "broken rung" in executive advancement. This panel moves beyond "survival" to offer a proactive Recession-Proof Toolkit. Attendees will learn how to audit their role's AI-vulnerability, build financial sovereignty through "Portfolio Careers," and leverage complex human leadership as their most un-automatable asset. The discussion will deliver actionable strategies for professional fortification, focused on skills, financial prudence, and radical self-nurturing.

sessions.title: Both Sides of the Table: Cracking Tech Interviews in the AI Era
sessions.abstract:
Everyone walks into technical interviews more prepared than ever. AI-generated solutions. Polished answers. Clean code. And yet — more candidates are getting rejected.
Because companies didn't lower the bar. They shifted it.
The coding round looks familiar. The scoring doesn't. What earns a hire decision today is reasoning out loud, defending your choices under follow-up, and navigating ambiguity in real time. These are exactly the things AI cannot do for you in
the room.
Two engineers — with 20+ years of combined experience and hundreds of interviews from both sides of the table — break down what has actually changed, what hasn't, and what a strong candidate looks like right now.
Across coding, system design, AI/ML design, and behavioral rounds, you'll learn exactly what separates a hire from a no-hire in the AI era — and leave with a concrete framework to prepare for each one.
You have AI. Now learn what to do with it.

It's a proven, battle-tested robust system trusted by some of the world’s most demanding distributed architectures. You will build a real workflow using native code and experience how durability, retries and fault tolerance come built-in.

Whether you're a backend engineer, distributed systems enthusiast, or reliability-focused developer, this session will demystify workflow orchestration and show how to design stateful, scalable systems you can rely on. Gain hands-on experience building production-grade, resilient services.

sessions.title: A11y All Week: Daily Practices for Developers
sessions.abstract: Web accessibility is not a one-time fix; it is a daily practice that directly shapes how users experience the digital world. With one in four U.S. adults living with a disability, developers have a meaningful opportunity to improve usability through small, consistent choices. This lecture introduces a simple weekly framework designed to make accessibility skills easier to build and maintain. Seven practical techniques, each immediately applicable, will be demonstrated to provide a repeatable routine that helps accessibility become a natural part of the development process. Participants will learn how decisions like semantic code structure, thoughtful color selection, and effective navigation patterns contribute to more inclusive user experiences. By strengthening these foundational skills, attendees will be better equipped to create digital products that are reliable, user friendly, and accessible to all.

sessions.title: AI Didn't Give Me Answers. It Gave Me Standing.
sessions.abstract:
Earlier this year my father broke his hip. At his age and with his complications, he was facing a 50% mortality rate. I took two months of leave and moved back to Oregon to care for him.

I am a data scientist, not a clinician, and I did not understand a single line of his medical records when I started reading them. By the end of those two months I had found a diagnosis that had been sitting in his chart for two years, reversed the malnutrition that was slowly starving him, gotten him hearing aids he had refused for years, moved him somewhere better, and more than doubled his income through a VA claim that 70% of applicants lose.

AI did not make me smarter. It made me credible enough to keep asking after his doctor told me no three times.

I will walk through what I did, where it got things wrong, and how to build that fluency now, before you are the one sitting in the hospital chair.

sessions.title: Don't Panic! Your First On-Call Survival Guide
sessions.abstract:
RING RING RING
It’s 2:07 AM. Your phone is buzzing. Production is on fire. Dashboards are red. Customers are impacted. You’re on-call.
For many new engineers, on-call is the first time you truly own a real-time production issue — one that affects real users, real money, and real business outcomes. It’s exciting…but honestly a little terrifying.
While many teams provide technical onboarding, new engineers still often feel unprepared for the real-world pressures they’re going to face. In this workshop, we’ll introduce what actually happens during on-call, explore how to respond when alerts fire, and give tips on writing clear post-mortems. Afterwards, you’ll get a chance to practice these skills in an engaging, interactive incident simulation where you will face realistic incidents, make decisions, and learn that there are no perfect answers, only thoughtful trade-offs.
Join us for this workshop to build confidence as you practice triaging issues and communicating clearly under pressure.

Through honest stories, practical advice, and lessons learned along the way, we’ll explore how past experiences can become a strength when stepping back into tech.
Attendees will leave with a clearer sense of how to close skill gaps, regain momentum, and approach the first months back with intention. Whether you’re getting hands-on, moving into delivery or project management, or figuring out where you fit in today’s industry, this session offers a real-world perspective on making a successful return.

sessions.title: Stand Out in the Stack: Writing Technical Achievements That Sell Your Skills
sessions.abstract: You've built the skills, but is your job search strategy working as hard as you are? Landing a tech role takes more than technical ability; it demands a compelling resume, a strategic LinkedIn presence, and a focused search plan. Yet many students and early-career professional struggle: generic resumes get filtered out by applicant tracking systems, LinkedIn profiles sit dormant, and searches feel aimless. In this workshop we tackle all three. We start with resume fundamentals: structuring a technical resume that passes ATS screening, quantifying impact with strong bullet points, and tailoring to target roles. Next, LinkedIn strategy: optimizing your headline, summary, and skills for recruiter visibility, building presence, and leveraging connections. Then participants bring their resume for a live peer review using a structured rubric. Attendees leave with a polished resume, an actionable LinkedIn optimization checklist, and a focused 30-day job search action plan.

Participants will leave with a clearer understanding of what it takes to lead at the executive level in AI, including the leadership skills, decision-making mindset, and strategic influence required to move beyond technical expertise and into enterprise leadership.

sessions.title: Built for Billions: Engineering Financial Inclusion at Scale
sessions.abstract:

For the teams building those systems, the complexity is just as real: regulatory environments that actively conflict across borders, fragmented API standards, and infrastructure constraints that no single architecture solves cleanly.

PayPal is tackling this head -on by building a global platform connecting the largest countries, billions of users, and merchants worldwide. Mudita Tiwari, Global Head of Product Management, will walk through the real tradeoffs: how to architect interoperable systems that connect markets, bring complex partner ecosystems together, navigate conflicting regulations, and deploy AI responsibly while currency moves across the world in real time. 

She'll share her path from developer to consultant to fintech product leader, and what it taught her about building for global scale without losing sight of the person on the other end of the transaction.

sessions.title: Data Is the Model: Rethinking How We Build AI Systems
sessions.abstract:
As AI systems become more powerful, the spotlight often lands on flashy models and new tools, while data is treated as a prerequisite rather than a defining component. In reality, AI systems behave the way they do because of the data they are trained on, not just the algorithms behind them.
This session takes a data-first look at how AI systems are really built, drawing on real-world datasets, applied machine learning projects, and classroom experience. Attendees will see how data quality, representation, imbalance, and context directly shape AI performance, reliability, and trust. Using concrete examples, the talk surfaces common data pitfalls that often go unnoticed and shows how they can derail even the most sophisticated models.
By shifting the focus from “Which model should I use?” to “What data is shaping this system?”, participants will leave with a more practical, responsible, and sustainable approach to building AI.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

This session will provide a framework for breaking into a technical role within an organization without starting over. Based on the speaker's real-world experience in leading HR technology, analytics, and platform initiatives, the speaker will share the tools and mindset required for breaking into a technical role within an organization.

sessions.title: Building Fast, Intentional MVPs: A Framework for Strategic Execution
sessions.abstract:
Senior engineering leaders face a critical tension when building MVPs: move fast or build it right? This session delivers a framework for making strategic technical decisions while empowering your teams to execute quickly without creating unmaintainable systems.
Through a case study where my team built end-to-end video capabilities in 16 weeks, achieving double-digit engagement increases and becoming the foundation for multiple company-wide features, you'll learn systematic approaches for evaluating "hack vs invest" trade-offs, choosing which organizational dependencies to bypass, and aligning teams around a technical vision that accelerates delivery.
This is a reusable methodology you can teach your teams and apply across domains: video platforms, ML systems, payment infrastructure, or any 0-to-1 initiative. You'll leave with practical decision tools, strategies for navigating organizational complexity, and leadership practices for maintaining team alignment under tight timelines.

sessions.title: Making Presentations Land: Structure, Slides, and Social Styles

Led by data and AI executives Vivien Wong and Abimbola Anifowoshe, the session focuses on practical fundamentals like clarifying purpose, designing narrative flow, and using slides to reduce cognitive load rather than add it. Participants will also explore the social styles framework, expressive, driver, analytical, and amiable to understand how different audiences interpret information and persuasion.

Through guided hands-on exercises, attendees will adapt real presentations for different audiences and styles. The goal is not polish, but impact: clearer thinking, stronger signal, and presentations that move decisions forward.

sessions.title: From Self-Care to Squad-Care: Elevating Women’s Wellbeing in the Workplace
sessions.abstract:
Women in tech don’t lack ambition, talent, or drive. They operate inside systems that ask them to carry more while offering less in return. From invisible labor and pay gaps to burnout and barriers to advancement, these challenges rarely respond to individual effort alone. Yet much of the advice women receive still centers on self-optimization instead of structural support.

This workshop reframes wellbeing as a collective practice. Through the lens of five dimensions of workplace wellness—career, financial, community, emotional, and physical—participants will explore how connection, not just resilience, drives sustainable success. Together, we will identify the patterns that hold women back and shift toward “squad care” as a strategy for shared growth, advocacy, and advancement. Attendees will leave with practical tools to support one another, navigate workplace realities with greater clarity, and build networks that move from connection to action. Because the path forward doesn’t rely on doing more alone. It depends on how effectively we show up for each other.

sessions.title: Adaptive Access: How AI is Transforming IAM Security
sessions.abstract:
Organizations increasingly rely on identity as the security perimeter, but static IAM fails against modern attacks like MFA fatigue, credential stuffing, and insider threats. This session demonstrates how AI-driven adaptive access evaluates User → Device → Location → Behavior → Risk Score → Policy Decision in real time, enabling context-aware, risk-based access. 

Attendees will explore real-world breaches, practical frameworks for implementing adaptive IAM, and learn how AI strengthens Zero Trust, reduces false positives, and transforms identity security from reactive to proactive. 

Key takeaway: Adaptive IAM continuously validates trust.
tracks: Technical Deep Dives (AI/ML, Engineering, Data, Security, etc.)

sessions.title: Inclusive Leadership without a title
sessions.abstract:
Leadership does not begin with a title, a team, or organizational authority. It begins with how we help the people around us contribute, learn, and succeed.

Drawing from experiences leading teams across the United States, Japan, and India, this session explores how individuals at every career stage can practice inclusive leadership. Attendees will learn how to share context instead of hoarding knowledge, create space for questions and different communication styles, support colleagues across time zones and cultures, and turn even overlooked assignments into opportunities to build trust and multiply the capabilities of others.

The session will also examine how AI can reduce language and information barriers through translation, accessible presentations, clearer communication, and personalized learning—while recognizing that technology cannot replace curiosity, cultural understanding, empathy, or accountability.

Through personal stories and practical examples, attendees will leave with behaviors they can apply immediately: approaching their work with ownership, asking the question others may be afraid to ask, bringing colleagues into the learning journey, and leaving every team more capable than they found it. Because inclusive leadership is not about being at the center—it is about making the room larger and bringing others with you.

sessions.title: Building Agentic AI Systems That Don’t Break: From Data Pipelines to Product Decisions
sessions.abstract:
Agentic AI is rapidly moving from experimentation into production, powering workflows, decision engines, and automation. Yet many systems fail not because of weak models, but because teams underestimate the hidden work across product design, data readiness, and system reliability.

In this session, a Product Manager, Data Engineer, and AI Engineer share how agentic systems are built end-to-end — from defining user problems and preparing retrieval-ready data to orchestrating tools, evaluation, guardrails, and monitoring in production. Drawing on real industry lessons, we highlight where agent pipelines most often break and how cross-functional teams can prevent these failures.

Attendees will learn a practical framework for aligning product, data, and AI roles, designing reliable agent workflows, and deploying AI systems that remain trustworthy, measurable, and useful over time.

sessions.title: Beyond the Buzzwords: Early-Career Engineers Building Real Impact with AI
sessions.abstract:
What does it really mean to build with AI as an early-career engineer? In this session, we’ll share our experiences navigating the transforming landscape of Software Engineering (SWE) and Machine Learning Engineering (MLE) across various tech companies, including Google, Microsoft, and Nike.
First, we will compare and contrast our experiences with our roles and companies. We’ll begin by clarifying how these roles differ and where they increasingly overlap as AI evolves. We’ll explore how AI is reshaping day-to-day work, from accelerating development to enabling entirely new capabilities, while also unpacking where it falls short. Between model hallucinations and reliability concerns, and the real costs of deploying AI systems compared to traditional automation, we’ll examine the trade-offs engineers must consider. Finally, we’ll discuss how companies evaluate AI usage and measure impact across a range of business goals.

sessions.title: Plot Twist: Career Strategy, Confidence & the Power of Networking
sessions.abstract: Early-career professionals are often told to "stay in their lane," yet strategic pivots accelerate growth when done intentionally — and with confidence in what you already bring. This session provides a practical blueprint for bold career moves early in tech while reducing risk. We reframe common fears — feeling too junior, losing credibility, not being ready — because your skills and perspective are more transferable than you think. We introduce the Early Career Pivot Triangle (Skill Depth, Business Impact, Relationship Capital) and a 4-step framework: clarify what energizes you, translate existing skills, prototype before switching, and build relationship capital early. Presenters share real journeys from distinct backgrounds — honest, not aspirational. We also share tactical LinkedIn networking strategies that go beyond the job board, helping you build the right relationships before roles are even posted. Attendees leave with a structured decision model, a downloadable Career Pivot Action Sheet, and the confidence to pursue stretch opportunities on their own terms.

sessions.title: Alignment before Optimization: 7 Skills to Navigate Uncertainty in Today's Evolving Tech Careers
sessions.abstract:
For decades, career advancement in technology was driven by optimization: improving performance, gaining experience, and progressing along predictable paths. As AI and structural shifts reshape technical work, optimization alone is no longer sufficient. Alignment—the ability to detect change early and calibrate your trajectory accordingly—has become a critical career skill.

This talk translates insights from navigating product lead roles at Microsoft, Snap, and Amazon, and a nonlinear career sabbatical, into 7 concrete skills attendees can apply immediately. Attendees will leave with practical tools to navigate uncertainty and build resilient, future-aligned careers.

sessions.title: 10 Strategies for Using AI to Improve Your Thinking
sessions.abstract:
You'll leave with a new way of working — one where AI makes you more you, not less. AI is no longer just a tool — it's a thinking partner. 

Use AI to ask better questions, not just get faster answers ·  Identify blind spots, assumptions, and trade‑offs using AI prompts ·  Apply AI to structured thinking (planning, evaluation, decision reviews) ·  Maintain human accountability, judgment, and agency in AI‑assisted work ·  Evaluate when AI adds value—and when it does not

The real gap isn't access to AI; it's knowing how to think with it. This talk challenges the idea that AI replaces work and reframes it: AI should sharpen your thinking, not outsource it. The focus isn't prompts or tools — it's developing the mindset to lead, decide, and create with AI while holding onto human accountability and agency.

In this session, an AI Product Manager shares what it actually looks like to think with AI in high-stakes, technical environments — not as a shortcut, but as a force multiplier for judgment. Drawing from real experience building and deploying AI systems, this talk offers a practical framework for using AI to surface what you're missing, stress-test what you believe, and move forward with more clarity and confidence.

sessions.title: 3×Faster Delivery: A PM–Design–Engineering Operating Model with Visual Development Tools
sessions.abstract: Visual development tools can unlock major speed gains, but without the right operating model they can create inconsistent UX, governance gaps, accessibility regressions, and “shadow changes” outside engineering controls. This presentation shares a leadership-ready approach to achieve 3× delivery velocity for Product–Design–Engineering teams using visual development tools while maintaining quality, security, brand consistency, and operational excellence. You’ll learn what work should be design-led vs engineering-led, how to set guardrails (design system constraints, permissions, review/approval flows, content rules), when to use human-in-the-loop oversight, and how to measure impact with a scorecard (cycle time, rework rate, defect escape, accessibility compliance, experiment throughput). We’ll cover a rollout strategy (pilot → scale) for strategic transformation, and leave you with a repeatable framework and checklist to ship faster without losing trust or control.

sessions.title: Beyond Scale: How Data Engineering Shapes Foundation Model Performance at Spotify
sessions.abstract:
Foundation models are only as strong as the datasets they're trained on but scale alone isn't enough. At Spotify, we learned that how you design your data matters as much as how much of it you have. As a technical lead and product manager on Spotify's AI Foundation team, we'll share our journey building the data foundation for LPM, Spotify's large personalization model powering personalization across Spotify's global user base. We'll explore the technical and product decisions behind data representation, signal selection, and dataset composition and what it takes to get those decisions right when a single model serves multiple products simultaneously.

Attendees will learn:

- How data design decisions - representation, sampling, and composition shape what a foundation model can and can't do

- How to build feedback loops between data changes and model outcomes when your evaluation framework is still maturing

sessions.title: 600 Billion Requests and Counting: Engineering Feature Flags at Massive Scale
sessions.abstract:
Wayfair’s global commerce platform serves 22M+ active customers and operates at massive scale. At this level, feature flags are not just deployment tools—they sit directly on the critical request path.

This session presents the architecture behind a high-throughput feature flag platform processing 17–18K requests per second at baseline and scaling beyond 100K RPS while maintaining sub-10ms tail latency. In a single year, the system served 6+ billion requests, supporting 400+ projects and thousands of active production flags.

We will walk through the evolution from a monolith-bound solution to a distributed Unleash-based architecture with regional clusters, Edge proxy layers, Redis-backed caching, autoscaling, and service mesh integration. The focus is on managing P99 and P99.9 latency at scale, reducing network hops, and building fail-safe systems that remain resilient under sustained high traffic.

sessions.title: Leaders Don't Wait for Titles: Building Your Web of Influence
sessions.abstract:
You work hard every single day. You have the ambition, the potential, and the drive to make an impact. But maybe the opportunities pass you by, or you find yourself pushed in a direction that doesn't reflect who you are. You know you’re meant for greater things, yet you don't know where to start or how to get there.

I've been there, and this is how I moved forward.

In this session, I share how I went from a new graduate to a recognized leader at work (and beyond) by serving my community of women in tech. What started as a desire to connect early career professionals with senior leaders who had been through the women in tech journey, quickly grew into something bigger. I built informal authority without a formal leadership title, allowing me to expand my network and influence. Through that journey, I recognized the importance of the 3Cs: Clarity, Communication, and Courage. These are three principles I now apply to every major decision in my life and career.

Explore how to apply the 3Cs to your current role and expand outward to build a network of relationships and experiences that creates opportunities for growth. This session gives you a reframed perspective on what you can do with what you already have and to set yourself up for the opportunities you are looking for.

Growth has never been linear. It's all about branching out, showing up genuinely, and building a web that lets opportunities find you.

sessions.title: Beyond Prompting: Fine-Tune Your Domain-Specific Language Model
sessions.abstract:
Prompt engineering is powerful, but it has limits. As AI systems move into real-world applications, domain adaptation becomes essential. Fine-tuning allows you to adapt a general purpose language model into a specialized model that performs more reliably on tasks in your domain.

In this hands-on workshop, participants will learn how to fine-tune a language model using parameter-efficient techniques (LoRA). We will walk through preparing data, running a lightweight training job, and evaluating measurable performance improvements.

Participants will leave with a working fine-tuning template, practical evaluation skills, and a reusable process they can apply to any domain, whether building AI tools, internal automation systems, or production-grade applications.

One day I'm working with a healthcare startup, next day a cybersecurity firm- building cross-industry experience few career paths can match. We will explore how this role functions as a technical partnership, requiring a unique blend of architectural depth and consultative skill — and the kind of problems you  get to solve everyday. Whether you are an early-career engineer or an aspiring architect, you'll walk away with a concrete understanding of this path, what makes it different, and what it takes to pursue it.

sessions.title: Your Work Makes Sense. But Does Its Story Translate?
sessions.abstract:
We talk about storytelling as something we do intentionally. But in tech, most stories are told unintentionally. 

Unintentionally through a narrow lens of 'Requirements, Design, Build, Test, Deploy.'

This shows up in how we explain our work, how we introduce ourselves, what we choose to share, and what we leave unsaid. Over time and from listening to hundreds of stories, I closely saw strong technical work lose meaning when it isn’t made legible to others. Back to basics, communication is especially crucial now - With extensive channels of communication made possible into 2026, comes the compromise of diluting context through the very systems that carry it. 

How then, do we envision beyond the industry's default playbook for ways to craft and communicate work?

To redress, I didn't have to look far - In my sophomore year, as I walked into my algorithms class in the morning and Data Sciences class in the afternoon, I caught myself at Philosophy, Physics, and Math lectures in the evening. While some labeled this as 'lacking clarity' in what I want to pursue, I did it anyway. As this developed into way of flipping open my career cards one at a time, I realized something. All these fields of study weren't separate - They were loosely connected through patterns I hadn’t learned to name yet.

In fact, all areas of study described the same concept, just in different languages. That was my 'Aha' moment. 

I knew there was something special to understanding the basics that founded an area of study. Once I understood the underlying patterns in one, I could translate them across others. 

And without trying to, that way of thinking began to show up:

- In how I explained systems. 

- In the way I learned large concepts in emerging Tech. 

- And in the way I applied science to practically executing my vision. 

Ever since, one of my passions outside of the many hats I'm gradually wearing, is one that reframes the art of simple language to explain complex solutions that run the world around us. In very simple language. But one that stands out for uniquely being 'YOUR' perspective. 

 This session will take a fresh attempt at exploring storytelling in Tech - Storytelling not as self-promotion. But rather a form of professional responsibility. As a way to shape trust and credibility through everyday moments and bringing your unique blend of expertise in areas within and outside of tech.  

Because whether you intend to or not, you are shaping how others understand your work and your judgment every day.

Attendees will leave with practical ways to:

1.  Communicate complex work with clarity and precision

2. Navigating multiple careers simultaneously.

3. Strategically position knowledge from different domains into your technical work. 

4. Most importantly, create a presence that reflects the quality of your judgement: Not just the output. 

Because while it's your technical skills that get you in the door, a muscle that pushes you beyond the finish line is the art of intentional, simple, and structured storytelling of your work - Within and outside of Tech

sessions.title: Building Human-Centered AI in Healthcare Customer Service with Abbott Diabetes Care
sessions.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence is transforming industries, but its greatest potential is realized when it empowers people to make a greater impact. In healthcare, that impact can extend far beyond technology, it can help improve the experience of people managing chronic health conditions every day.

In this session, discover how Abbott's Customer Service innovation was able to harness AI-powered agent assistance, intelligent customer intake, speech analytics, and automation to create faster, more personalized, and more meaningful customer interactions. What began as an ambitious digital transformation initiative has grown into a solution supporting thousands of specialized customer service agents while delivering measurable improvements in both operational performance and customer experience.

More than a technology story, this is a story of collaboration, innovation, and purpose. Attendees will gain an inside look at how teams across technology, business, quality, and customer service came together to design, deploy, and scale AI responsibly within a highly regulated healthcare environment. Through real-world lessons and practical insights, the session will explore how to build trust in AI, lead transformational change, measure business value, and balance innovation with compliance and patient-centered outcomes.

Whether you're a software engineer, architect, product leader, data professional, or aspiring technology innovator, you'll leave with a powerful example of how technology can solve meaningful problems at scale while keeping people at the center. Join us to learn how human-centered AI is shaping the future of healthcare, and what it takes to turn bold ideas into solutions that make a lasting difference.

sessions.title: Engineering the In-Between: Educating Artful Engineers for Complex Futures
sessions.abstract: Today's most pressing challenges (e.g., climate change, public health, social inequity, digital transformation) are not engineering problems alone. They are human problems that require different (i.e., more artful) design approaches. This session brings together a diverse panel of academics and practitioners from engineering, computer science, architecture, and design from across the globe. Each bridges disciplines, sectors, and ways of knowing to enact technological know-how with business acumen and human understanding, ensuring not only better design today but more well-equipped designers for tomorrow. Individually, they will share their unusual yet inspiring career trajectories, while reflecting on lessons learned and brainstorming thoughts on how best to design for complex futures. Together, they will advocate for multi/inter/transdisciplinary praxis, practice, and pedagogy--elevating the art and science behind design, balancing technical rigor with business strategy, and ensuring social valuation and creation. 'Engineering the In-Between' is geared toward learners and leaders across the Triple Helix of academia, industry, and government. The aim? To consider new ways of doing and learning, cultivate future multi/inter/transdisciplinarians who can conduct the creative and incisive work needed in the critical 'in-between,' and aim for transformative flourishing by design.

sessions.title: Leading Through Relentless Transformation: Strategy, Sanity, and Selective Control
sessions.abstract:
We keep treating transformation like a phase. It’s not a phase — it’s the environment.

AI acceleration, workforce shifts, and global instability have permanently altered the terrain of technology leadership. Yet many organizations still operate with industrial-era assumptions: maximize utilization, plan extensively, and control tightly. Those systems were built for predictability. We no longer live there.

This session explores how leaders can redesign decision-making, funding, and ownership for constant change. Participants will learn how to anchor in clear strategic outcomes while enabling adaptive execution; make invisible work and bureaucratic friction visible; simplify ownership to accelerate momentum; and fund initiatives like a venture portfolio, not a factory pipeline.

In a world of relentless disruption, leaders must stabilize what matters most — trust, transparency, and direction — and release the illusion of control everywhere else.

sessions.title: Next-Gen Leaders: Leadership Shifts for AI-Accelerated Engineering Teams
sessions.abstract:
As AI accelerates code generation, the challenge for engineering teams shifts from slow delivery to erosion of architectural ownership, decision quality, and critical context. When execution becomes abundant, leadership must evolve to effectively lead hybrid teams of humans and AI agents.

My transition from Senior Engineer to Team Lead revealed that leadership habits that once drove success can now create hidden risk in AI-accelerated teams. This session introduces a Leadership Playbook for the Age of AI – a modern framework built around five essential executive leadership shifts, such as moving from scaling execution to scaling judgment, from architectural control to decision guardrails, and from growing coders to growing decision-makers.

Through this talk, we will explore each principle and the mindset shifts behind them. Attendees will leave with a practical playbook that is designed to help them lead with clarity when speed is easy, but good decisions are not.

This interactive workshop helps women leaders and aspiring leaders navigate these double binds using Emotional Intelligence (EI) and the principles of Whole Human Leadership. Participants identify common triggers, examine habits that hold them back, and practice emotionally intelligent responses through guided exercises and role‑play. The session blends evidence‑based EI insights with practical tools for mentorship, sponsorship, and high‑stakes workplace conversations, expanding leadership to address human, social, and systemic complexity.
Attendees leave with ready‑to‑use language, a mentorship conversation framework, and a 30‑day habit experiment they can apply immediately in meetings and feedback discussions.

The unemployment rate for Black women rose significantly from the start of 2025 to December. More than 300,000 Black Women lost their jobs, and that number is growing. This narrative extends beyond mere statistics: it embodies a profound journey of healing, resilience, reinvention, and policy reform. The emotional toll of job loss can lead to issues such as mental health struggles. Yet, amidst these challenges, Black women often emerge as powerful agents of change. This panel discussion hopes to foster a holistic dialogue that acknowledges the challenges and celebrates the resilience and ingenuity that women bring to the workforce. It will illuminate pathways to recovery and power, showcasing approaches to redefine careers in tech and beyond.

sessions.title: Connect Your Dots: Turn Your Experience into the Job You Want
sessions.abstract:
We’ve all heard the anecdote: women often apply to a role only when they meet 100% of a job description, while men will apply at 60% of criteria met. This session isn’t a pep talk to “just apply anyway” or to “shoot your shot”. Instead, this session is about helping you recognize that you are likely far more qualified than you think. You’re often much closer to meeting all that job criteria than you realize.

“Connecting Your Dots” is a strategy I’ve taught through internal talks within Electronic Arts and throughout the gaming industry. The goal is to show how experience that doesn’t match a job description word-for-word is often still highly relevant. Through your resume, cover letter, and interviews, the responsibility falls on you to connect that experience to what’s being sought after. This session equips you with practical skills to do exactly that, because no one else will connect those dots for you.

sessions.title: Excellent at Everything… Except Relaxing: A Nervous System Upgrade for Women in Tech
sessions.abstract:
You can debug production issues at 2am, lead teams, mentor junior engineers, and navigate bias. All before lunch! But when it comes to relaxing, your nervous system didn’t get the memo. Every Slack ping feels like a five-alarm fire.

High-performing women in tech are running on adrenaline, cortisol, and sheer force of will. Tight chest, racing thoughts, sleep on backorder, and caffeine acting like critical infrastructure. We’ve normalized white-knuckling our way through the day, hoping ambition will sustain us.

This interactive session is your performance upgrade. Plot twist: calm is not weakness. It’s a competitive advantage. Backed by real science and built for real life, you’ll learn how 10 minutes a day of intentional nervous system regulation can level up your focus, stabilize energy, improve sleep, and strengthen emotional control without slowing you down.

Get a clear, practical understanding of stress physiology in high-demand environments and experience a live reset you can deploy in real time before a presentation, negotiation, or that meeting you’re already dreading.

Advancing women in tech isn’t only about access. It’s about longevity. You don’t need to quit tech or become a monk. You need a nervous system that can support your ambition.

sessions.title: The Science of Visibility: Embodied Personal Power in Technical Leadership
sessions.abstract:
Technical excellence earns a seat at the table. Embodied power determines whether you speak once seated.
Research in embodied cognition and personal sense of power shows that what we wear and how we physically present ourselves influences cognitive performance, decisiveness, and risk tolerance. At the same time, shame research and Daring Leadership work highlight that visibility requires values alignment, boundaries, and grounded confidence.
This session introduces a research-informed framework built on four Image Needs—Alignment, Authority, Safety, and Expression—to help women in tech reduce self-monitoring, strengthen executive presence, and increase leadership visibility without sacrificing authenticity.
Participants will leave with practical tools to use personal image as a behavioral reinforcement system for high-stakes moments: promotions, presentations, negotiations, and C-level transitions.

sessions.title: Who Is Responsible When AI Is Wrong? Break, Test, and Secure a Live AI Agent
sessions.abstract:
We built an AI agent for a bank. In a demo, it's flawless. In the real world, it's a liability, and most teams wouldn't catch why until it's too late. 

AI failures aren't dramatic. They're subtle, confident, and expensive. The model doesn't crash. It fabricates an answer that sounds perfect. It doesn't throw an error. It quietly leaks data to someone who knew the right thing to type. And when it goes wrong, your customers pay the price. 

In this highly interactive workshop, three practitioners work alongside you through live polls, hands-on exercises, and cross-role debriefs to stress-test a live AI agent. You'll evaluate it for hallucinations, red team it with prompt injection attacks to extract sensitive data, identify high-risk automation decisions and harms that ship when nobody's looking. 

Whether you're an engineer, PM, or leader, you'll walk out with frameworks to catch these failures and the confidence to own them. 

No ML experience needed. Just a laptop and curiosity.
